body:
## Summary
Builds on Phase 4a PR2 (#91, already merged) — that PR shipped notes, internal_tags, the audit table, inline `EditableField`, `AddressEditDialog`, `ServiceLocationEditDialog`, `EditHistoryPanel`, and a basic sqft → crew_strategy cascade. **Phase 4b expands the surface and makes cascade handling first-class.**

- Centralized `_lib/analysis/edit-cascade.ts` with rule-driven module-staling and effects payloads written into the audit row
- Service-location whitelist expanded from **5 → 12 fields** (visit/hours overrides, crew override, contract value, custom_fields, service_offering_id, etc.)
- `CascadeBanner` on Property Detail names the staled modules and links to the analysis dashboard
- `CustomFieldsEditor` — generic key/value jsonb editor used for SL `custom_fields`
- New admin pages: account-wide audit log (paginated, filterable) + properties admin list with bulk edit
- POST `/api/properties/bulk-edit` for add-tag / remove-tag / set-notes across many properties

## Schema (`supabase/migrations/20260430042852_phase4b_audit_extensions.sql`)
Additive only — kept the existing 4a PR2 table shape:

```sql
ALTER TABLE property_edit_history
  ADD COLUMN reason TEXT,
  ADD COLUMN cascading_effects JSONB;
```

The 4b spec called for `entity_type` + `entity_id` discriminator columns, but the existing `property_id` + `service_location_id` columns are functionally equivalent (entity_type is derivable from "service_location_id IS NULL"). Migrating would invalidate existing rows for no behavioral gain.

## Cascade rules (`api/_lib/analysis/edit-cascade.ts`)
| Field changed | Modules staled | Other effects |
|---|---|---|
| Property address (any of 6) | crew_strategy + bid + drive_time + branch_opt | re-geocode (already 4a) |
| `serviceable_sqft` (≥10%) | crew + workforce + bid | — |
| `service_offering_id` | **all tier-2** | clear `property_comparables` cache |
| `visits_per_year_override` / `hours_per_visit_override` | crew + bid | — |
| `crew_size_override` | crew | — |
| `monthly_contract_value` | bid | — |

`applyCascadingEffects` flips `portfolio_analyses.status='stale'` for the most-recent completed row of each staled module and calls `triggerSynthesisRefresh` (debounced).

## Service-location field whitelist (now 12)
Existing 5 (display_name, location_code, suite_or_floor, serviceable_sqft, status) **+** `service_frequency`, `visits_per_year_override`, `hours_per_visit_override`, `crew_size_override`, `monthly_contract_value`, `frequency_notes`, `custom_fields`, `service_offering_id`.

`service_schedule` (jsonb) kept read-only — rich scheduler editor is Phase 4f. `monthly_direct_cost` / `crew_size` / `site_contact_*` / `access_notes` from the spec deferred — would need new schema columns; not worth a migration when those fields aren't used by any module yet.

## API
- `PATCH /api/v1/properties/[id]` — now also accepts `edit_reason`; response carries `cascading_effects: { analyses_marked_stale, synthesis_refresh_triggered, comparables_invalidated, reasons }` and `edits_recorded`
- `PATCH /api/v1/service-locations/[id]` — same shape, expanded whitelist
- `GET /api/accounts/[accountId]/clients/[clientId]/edit-history` — paginated audit feed; filters: `entity_type`, `field_name`, `edited_by` (substring), `date_from`/`date_to`, `has_cascading_effects`, `page`, `limit` (max 200)
- `POST /api/properties/bulk-edit` — body `{ property_ids[], action: 'add_tag'|'remove_tag'|'set_notes', value }`. Append-style semantics — already-tagged properties are skipped, returned as `unchanged`. Caps at 500 properties/call.

## UI
- `ServiceLocationEditDialog` rewritten to render all 12 fields dynamically from the whitelist + offering select populated from `/api/v1/service-offerings` + sqft-stale and offering-change warnings inline + optional reason field
- `CascadeBanner` (12s auto-dismiss) above PropertyDetail naming staled modules with a "Re-run modules →" link to the analysis dashboard
- `CustomFieldsEditor` — chip-style key/value rows + add row + delete; auto-converts numeric strings so jsonb numeric queries keep working
- `/admin/audit-log` page with filter card (entity_type, edited_by, cascade-only) + paginated table (50/page) showing field labels, old → new diff chips, attribution, and a cascade badge with stale-count
- `/admin/properties` page with checkbox per row + select-all-filtered + action bar (Add tag / Remove tag / Set notes) + dialog for the action's value
- `AnalysisSidebar` gains nav links to all three admin pages (Properties admin, Constraint templates, Edit history)

## Trade-offs
- **No table-shape migration.** Spec wanted `entity_type`/`entity_id`; current schema has `property_id` + `service_location_id`. Equivalent, kept to preserve existing audit rows.
- **No bulk action for arbitrary fields.** `bulk-edit` covers tags + notes only — that's the practical 90%. Other fields stay per-row.
- **`monthly_direct_cost` and `crew_size` are NOT in the whitelist** because they don't exist as columns. Spec listed them but no module reads them. Deferring schema additions until something actually needs them.
- **Cascade applies on the next dashboard interaction**, not in-line. We mark stale; the existing dashboard polling kicks foreground re-runs. No new infra needed.

## Test plan
- [ ] Edit a service location's `serviceable_sqft` from 10000 → 11500 (15%) → SaveBanner appears: "Crew Strategy, Workforce Sizing, Bid Pricing marked stale" with Re-run link
- [ ] Edit `service_offering_id` to a different offering → CascadeBanner names all tier-2 modules + "Comparables cache cleared"
- [ ] Edit only `frequency_notes` → no cascade banner (no modules staled)
- [ ] Add a `reason` ("Sqft corrected after walkthrough") → audit log row carries the reason
- [ ] Open `/admin/audit-log` → see recent edits, filter by `has_cascading_effects=true` → only edits that staled modules
- [ ] Filter audit log by `edited_by=jon@` → narrows to user
- [ ] Open `/admin/properties` → list of all properties with tags
- [ ] Filter "high-priority" → narrows
- [ ] Select 5 properties → "Add tag" → enter "vip-2026" → all 5 get tagged → result toast: "5 updated · 0 unchanged · 0 missing"
- [ ] Select the same 5 again → "Add tag" → "vip-2026" again → "0 updated · 5 unchanged"
- [ ] Edit custom_fields on an SL → add `cleaning_frequency: weekly`, `key: 1234` → numeric value preserved as number
- [ ] DELETE existing comparables row, edit `service_offering_id` → comparables row cleared

author: gjeon03
body:
## Two reported issues, one root cause + one new one

**Issue 1 — textarea draft follows you across tabs.** Type in session A's chat composer, don't press Enter, switch to session B → A's text shows up in B's textarea.

**Issue 2 — Sync button disabled in other tabs.** Click Sync in session A, switch to session B → B's Sync button stays disabled until A's sync finishes.

Both root-cause to the same thing: in \`ProjectPage\`, switching tabs only changes \`activeSession\` and re-renders \`<ChatView session={activeSession} />\`. React reuses the same component instance and just updates props — \`useState(input)\` and \`useState(wikiSyncing)\` (and queue, attachments, runStartAt, etc.) all survive. Whatever state was set in session A is what session B sees.

## Fix part 1 — force remount per session

Pass \`key={activeSession.id}\` to \`ChatView\`, \`PinnedPanel\`, and \`BottomPanel\`. React unmounts the old instance and mounts a fresh one whenever the active session id changes. Every session-local piece of state starts clean.

## Fix part 2 — global wiki-sync lock (new follow-up)

Once the remount fix lands, the two Sync buttons across tabs become truly independent — meaning a user can now actually fire two syncs at once. That's a real concurrency hazard: the wiki is a single shared \`pages/\` tree, the sync agent reads a snapshot then issues writes via Edit/Write, and \`index.md\` is rewritten as part of every sync. Two agents running at the same time race on the snapshot and last-write-wins on overlapping pages.

Wiki sync also does cross-project routing (#29), so a per-project lock isn't enough — the safe primitive is a global single-flight lock.

\`runWikiSync\` now holds a process-wide \`activeSync\` reference. The second caller throws \`another wiki sync is already in progress (session X). Try again when it finishes.\` The frontend's existing error surfacing shows that message in its banner; no UI changes required.

Tradeoff: the user can't parallelize different-project syncs. In practice sync is short (~20-40s), and the cross-project routing makes "no two agents touch the same pages dir" the real invariant. Queue-and-wait is cheap and correct.

## Test plan

- [x] typecheck + build pass
- [ ] Manual: type in session A, switch to B without Enter — B's textarea is empty
- [ ] Manual: click Sync in A, switch to B before A finishes — B's Sync button is enabled (clicking it gets the locked error message in A's banner only after we navigate back)
- [ ] Manual: trigger sync in B while A still running — see "another wiki sync is already in progress" error
- [ ] Manual: confirm normal sequential sync still works (sync A, wait, sync B)

## Out of scope

- Show a global "wiki sync running" indicator that disables all Sync buttons everywhere (would need to surface \`activeSync\` to the frontend or use the notification store; deferred until the manual lock-rejection error is found insufficient).
- Move sync into the same notification rehydration pattern as analyze (also deferred).

## Summary

Adds [Astraflow](https://www.ucloud.cn/) (by UCloud / 优刻得) as a supported OpenAI-compatible provider. Astraflow is a model aggregation platform supporting 200+ models.

### What's changed

- **`headroom/providers/openai_compatible.py`**: Added two pre-configured factory functions:
  - `create_astraflow_provider()` — Global endpoint (`https://api-us-ca.umodelverse.ai/v1`), reads `ASTRAFLOW_API_KEY` from environment.
  - `create_astraflow_cn_provider()` — China endpoint (`https://api.modelverse.cn/v1`), reads `ASTRAFLOW_CN_API_KEY` from environment.

- **`headroom/providers/__init__.py`**: Exported both factory functions via `TYPE_CHECKING`, `__all__`, and `_LAZY_EXPORTS`.

### Usage

```python
import os
from headroom.providers import create_astraflow_provider

# Global endpoint
provider = create_astraflow_provider(api_key=os.environ["ASTRAFLOW_API_KEY"])

# China endpoint
from headroom.providers import create_astraflow_cn_provider
provider_cn = create_astraflow_cn_provider(api_key=os.environ["ASTRAFLOW_CN_API_KEY"])
```

Because Astraflow is fully OpenAI-compatible, no new SDK or subpackage is needed — this reuses the existing `OpenAICompatibleProvider` infrastructure.

author: jinwoo-h
body:
## Summary
- **Fix dead terminal after setup split**: `safeFit()` had a dimension-matching early-return that skipped `fitAddon.fit()` during pending splits — leaving the WebGL canvas stale after `wrapInSplit()` reparented the DOM. Now forces `fitAddon.fit()` + `terminal.refresh()` when `pendingSplitScrollState` is set, even when dimensions match.
- **Suppress noisy "no live transport" warning**: Added a 10s grace period after tab registration before logging the "saved PTY but no live transport" anomaly. The warning was firing on every mount because PTY spawn/attach is async — now it only warns if the transport is genuinely stuck.
- **Add `debugLabel` to PaneManager**: Logs now include `tab:<id>/wt:<id>` so safeFit warnings can be correlated to specific worktrees.
- **Add headful E2E stress tests**: 5 `@headful` test scenarios exercising the real setup-split flow with WebGL active — basic split, switch-back, rapid multi-worktree switching, forced WebGL context loss, and rapid switching during split lifecycle.

## Context
The dead terminal bug manifests as blank/unresponsive terminal panes after creating a worktree with a setup split. The PTY is alive (typing accepted), but the WebGL canvas never repaints. Cmd+R fixes it by replaying the daemon snapshot. Console logs show `[terminal] safeFit early-return during pending split for pane 1 — dims 136×89 match current, webgl: true` confirming the early-return codepath fires in production with WebGL active.

## Summary
- New `GET /api/v1/recipes/suggestions?count=4` returns up to 10 LLM-generated recipes shaped like `ExtractedRecipeDto`. The frontend can pass them straight into the existing save flow without translation.
- Triggered by the UI when collection matching (US-342) returns no/few results.
- Honors the user's dietary profile (US-301): `DietaryType` (vegetarian / vegan / pescatarian / …) + free-form `Restrictions[]` (gluten-free, lactose-free, …).

## Architecture
- New shared `IDietaryProfileProvider` (in `Yumney.Shared.Common`) returning a lightweight `DietaryProfileSnapshot` — same cross-module pattern as the existing `IIngredientBalanceProvider`. HTTP impl in Recipes.Infrastructure calls Users `/api/v1/users/me/profile`. 404 → `Empty` snapshot (unfiltered suggestions).
- New `IRecipeSuggestionService` (Application) + `SemanticKernelRecipeSuggestionService` (Extraction). System + user prompt with `<available_ingredients>` / `<dietary>` / `<count>` tags; JSON-repair retry on parse failure (mirrors the extraction service).
- AppHost: `recipesApi.WithReference(usersApi)` added so the new HTTP client resolves; `users-api` HTTP client wired in `RecipesInfrastructureServiceCollectionExtensions`.

## Closes
Closes #184 (US-343).

## Scope cuts
- **No streaming** — extraction has a streaming variant, suggestions stay synchronous for v1. LLM call ~2-3 s typically; fine for an explicit user-triggered action.
- **No caching** — suggestions are intentionally varied, caching is nuanced. Skip.
- **Dietary profile fields used:** `DietaryType` + `Restrictions[]` only. `WeeklyBalanceGoals` and `CookingEffort` are read but ignored in the prompt for v1.
- **Frontend deferred** — separate PR (will pair with US-342's frontend).
- **No prompt-shape unit test** for `SuggestionPrompts` — the prompt strings are intentionally simple constants; their behavior is exercised end-to-end via the handler tests.

body:
## Description

Fixes #9525

When a CLI agent session (e.g. Claude Code) completes, the tab title continued displaying the last permission request summary instead of the agent's final response. This happened because `title_like_text()` only consulted `self.summary`, which was set by `PermissionRequest` but never cleared by `Stop`, and `self.response` was set but never used for the title.

**Changes:**
- `title_like_text()` now falls back to `self.response` after `self.summary`, so completed sessions show the agent's final message
- The `Stop` handler now clears `self.summary` since it is no longer relevant after session completion
- Extracted a `trim_non_empty()` helper to deduplicate the trim-filter-own pattern across three call sites in the same module

## Testing

Added three new unit tests:
- `title_like_text_falls_back_to_response_when_summary_is_empty` — verifies response is used when summary is None
- `title_like_text_prefers_summary_over_response` — verifies summary takes precedence when both are present
- `display_title_shows_response_after_permission_request_then_stop` — regression test for the full PermissionRequest -> Stop flow

## Server API dependencies

N/A

CHANGELOG-BUG-FIX: Fix CLI agent tab title showing stale permission request text instead of agent response after session completes

### ✨ PR Description
## 1. Problem & Context

Prop-type migrations were running on every document load regardless of plugin version changes, wasting CPU on unnecessary cache invalidation. This fix ties invalidation to actual plugin updates via WordPress' upgrader hook.

## 2. What Changed (Where)

- **migrations-loader.php**: Transient TTL extended from 12 hours to 1 year (YEAR_IN_SECONDS)
- **migrations-orchestrator.php**: Added `maybe_invalidate_manifest_on_upgrade()` static method hooked to `upgrader_process_complete` to selectively invalidate manifest on Elementor/Pro updates
- **test-migrations-orchestrator.php**: New comprehensive test suite covering invalidation logic, plugin filtering, and singleton reset

## 3. How It Works

Hook fires after any WordPress plugin/theme/core upgrade → validates event is plugin update → checks if updated plugins list intersects with `['elementor/elementor.php', 'elementor-pro/elementor-pro.php']` → calls `Migrations_Loader::destroy()` to clear transient and reset singleton. Longer TTL means cached manifest persists across document loads until actual plugin version changes trigger invalidation.

## 4. Risks

Manifest could serve stale migrations if plugins update outside WordPress' upgrader (CLI, manual file replacement). Unlikely in managed environments but no mitigation provided. Transient key collision is theoretically possible but highly improbable given WordPress' namespacing conventions.

Nuclei scans (up to 180s) and ZAP scans (up to 300s) previously caused HTTP 524 errors from Cloudflare's ~100s connection timeout.

New approach: views return immediately with a job_id, the scan runs in a daemon thread, and the browser polls /control/jobs/<id>/ every 2 seconds until the result is ready. This keeps all HTTP requests well under any proxy timeout.

- utils/jobs.py: thread-safe in-process job queue (start_job, get_job) with automatic cleanup of jobs older than 1 hour
- admin_views.py + projects.py: manager_nuclei_scan, manager_nuclei_update, manager_zap_scan, manager_zap_update, project_nuclei_scan, nuclei_update_view, project_zap_scan, zap_update_view all become non-blocking — they start a background job and return {job_id}
- new job_poll_view at GET /control/jobs/<job_id>/
- JS in project_detail.html + manager_settings.html: pollJob() / mgrPollJob() helper polls until done, updates elapsed-time counter live while scan is running

author: nogate-ai
body:
## Summary

Implements the data-path RDC check we agreed on: per-flop reach-set analysis with async-reset flops as domain originators and sync/reset-none flops as transparent propagators. Lights up the 6 \`#[ignore]\` tests landed in PR #224 and clears \`tests/rdc/run_rdc.sh\`'s \`PHASE_2A_PENDING\` list.

## The rule

\`\`\`
reach[f] = { f.reset }            if f.reset_kind == Async
         = ⋃ reach[srcs]            otherwise

violation:
  f.Async       and any reach[src] contains a domain ≠ f.reset
  f.{Sync,None} and |reach[f]| > 1
\`\`\`

Each async reset signal originates its own domain by name. Sync and reset-none flops add no domain — they propagate whatever async domains reach their data input. The metastability chain only \"breaks\" at another async-reset flop.

## What's now caught (6 scenarios flipping from XFAIL to PASS)

| Test | Pattern | Why it flags now |
|---|---|---|
| **A2** | \`async/rst_a → async/rst_b\` direct | rb.async with rst_a in reach |
| **B1** | \`async → reset-none → async (different)\` | reset-none transparent; reach propagates |
| **B3** | \`async → sync → async (different)\` | sync transparent (option-1 semantic) |
| **C1** | two async sources converge at \`reset none\` | \`|reach[r]| > 1\` |
| **D2** | cross-clock + cross-async with data path | per-flop reach catches the cross-domain edge |
| **E2** | mutual feedback, two async domains | fixpoint converges, both flops trip |

## Implementation

\`src/typecheck.rs::check_rdc_phase2a\` (~200 LOC), called from \`check_module\`. Five steps:

1. **Build flop info** — for every \`reg\` decl + \`port reg\`, record (reset signal, reset kind, decl span). Fast-path early return if no async-reset flops exist.
2. **Compute let-binding transitive flop reads** via fixpoint — a \`let x = expr\` reading flop \`r\` means anyone reading \`x\` is effectively reading \`r\`.
3. **Build per-flop data-flow deps** — for each \`dst <= rhs\` in any seq block, intersect rhs's idents with the flop set; expand let names through their deps. Recurses into \`if\`/\`match\`/\`for\`.
4. **Compute reach via fixpoint** — async flops carry { self.reset } fixed; sync/none flops carry \`⋃ reach[deps]\` until stable.
5. **Per-flop violation check** — async flops flag if any source's reach has a foreign domain; sync/none flops flag if their own reach set has > 1 domain. Diagnostics point at the flop's decl span.

## \`pragma cdc_safe\` decision

Phase 2a is intentionally **not** gated on \`pragma cdc_safe;\`. That pragma silences CDC and the phase-1 cross-clock structural RDC check, but the data-path hazard is structurally distinct (single-clock multi-reset trips it without any CDC concern). A future \`pragma rdc_safe;\` annotation will be the dedicated opt-out — out of scope for this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] \`cargo test --release rdc_\` — 20 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored (6 previously-\`#[ignore]\`'d tests removed and lit up)
- [x] \`cargo test --release\` — **244 passed**, 0 failed (was 238 + 6 unignored)
- [x] \`tests/rdc/run_rdc.sh\` — 17 PASS, 0 XFAIL, 0 FAIL
- [x] \`examples/run_sims.sh -j8\` — **30/30 PASS** (no design example regresses under the stricter rule)
- [x] \`spec §5.4\` rewritten to document both phases + remaining phase-2b/2c/2d scope
- [x] \`COMPILER_STATUS.md\` updated: RDC entry now ✅ Phases 1+2a shipped; planned-features list updated to phases 2b–2d

## Follow-ups (separate PRs)

- **Phase 2b**: reset-driven clock gating (async-reset flop output → \`clkgate\` enable)
- **Phase 2c**: reconvergent RDC through synchronizers (reuses CDC reconvergence machinery)
- **Phase 2d**: cross-instance RDC + multi-source combiner glitch detection at port boundaries
- **\`pragma rdc_safe;\`**: per-module opt-out parallel to \`pragma cdc_safe;\`

## Summary

Static analysis of the pin-cycle pipeline (`nocturne-pin-cycle.path` → `nocturned cycle`) against Syncthing's sync behaviour. Adds `RACES.md` at the repo root with five races, each with `file:line` location, repro steps, and a concrete guard.

- **RACE-01 (HIGH)** — `nocturne-pin-cycle.path:12-13`, `ingest.c:533-535`, `atomic_io.c:112`: `PathChanged` fires when Syncthing creates `.syncthing.pins-phone-X.jsonl.tmp`, before the rename. Ingest reads the stale file, publishes manifest. When Syncthing renames, `PathChanged` fires again — but 1-second mtime resolution causes `JSONL.mtime == manifest.mtime`, so the gate check in `nocturne-pin-cycle-runner` suppresses the retry. New pin dropped until 15-min timer. Fix: nanosecond mtime comparison, or `.syncthing.*.tmp` sentinel check before starting the cycle.

- **RACE-02 (MEDIUM)** — `ingest.c:535`, `jsonl.c:130`: `open()` races Syncthing's atomic rename; ingest gets the old inode. Self-heals on retry, but only if RACE-01 gate passes.

- **RACE-03 (MEDIUM)** — `nocturne-cycle.service:9,13`, `watch.c:437`: inotify gap between watch stop/restart (`ExecStartPre`/`ExecStartPost --no-block`) lets Syncthing-delivered files land in `resident/` undetected. Files appear only after the 300-second periodic rescan. Fix: post-cycle `nocturned scan --subtree resident/`.

- **RACE-04 (LOW)** — `rotate.c:603,651,659`: crash between `unlink(archive/X)` and `track_repo_update_path` leaves track stuck — the existing EEXIST recovery path doesn't handle ENOENT. Fix: pending-move log row in SQLite.

- **RACE-05 (LOW)** — `ingest.c:533`, `jsonl.c:132`: persisted offset overshoots after phone app reinstall / Syncthing conflict reset shortens JSONL. Fix: `if (old_offset > st.st_size) old_offset = 0`.

## Changes

- `RACES.md` (new file, 246 lines) — analysis only, no code changes.

## Design choices documented here

- RACE-01 root cause is in `nocturne-pin-cycle-runner` (user-installed, not in repo). The fix options are spelled out in the doc so whoever edits that script can apply the right one.
- The `.tmp` sentinel approach in RACE-01 Option C is the most robust: it directly tests for the condition that causes the false trigger rather than trying to fix the timing of the gate check.
- RACE-04's ENOENT gap in `rotate.c`'s retry-convergence was previously undocumented; the existing comment at `rotate.c:17-25` covers EEXIST but not ENOENT.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `RACES.md` renders cleanly on GitHub
- [ ] Cross-reference each `file:line` against current source to confirm they match

## Summary

This PR resolves the final 3 merge conflicts between staging and main that persist after PR #176 merged.

## Conflicts Resolved

1. **.github/workflows/cla.yml** - Conflict between main's extended allowlist version and staging's simplified GITHUB_TOKEN-only version

Even after PR #176 merged to staging, PR #175 (staging→main) still shows conflicts because:
- staging-resolved branch was created BEFORE PR #176 merged
- staging has moved forward with the simplified CLA workflow
- AGENTS.md has additional content not in main

- Merge origin/main into it

body:
## Summary
- Adds a shared `tools::safe_client::build_validated_client` helper that pre-flights the configured base URL through `SsrfValidator::resolve_and_validate` and pins the resolved addrs via `reqwest::ClientBuilder::resolve_to_addrs` (DNS-rebind mitigation), reusing the pattern already in `http_request` / `web_fetch`.
- Replaces the four raw `reqwest::Client::new()` sites called out by bead `sera-rdg4`: `tools::spawn`, `tools::tool_search` (×2), `tools::knowledge` (×2), `tools::centrifugo`. A loopback / RFC-1918 / link-local / cloud-metadata override of the configured `SERA_CORE_URL` (or Centrifugo base URL) is now rejected before any connection attempt.
- No protocol payloads, gateway dispatch, or auth changed — surgical refactor of client construction only.

## Why
Bead `sera-rdg4` (and the agent-harness security report from 2026-04-29) flagged that runtime tool modules were constructing raw HTTP clients against operator-supplied base URLs without going through the existing SSRF validator, leaving an LLM-controlled override path to internal hosts / cloud metadata.

## Tests
- Helper-level negative coverage: loopback v4 (`127.0.0.1`), loopback v6 (`[::1]`), RFC-1918 `10/172/192`, link-local `169.254/16`, cloud metadata `169.254.169.254`, hostname resolving to loopback (`localhost`), and malformed URL.
- Helper-level positive: `accepts_public_ip_literal` proves a public IP literal builds a `Client` through the same code path.
- `pinned_addrs_route_to_mock_server` exercises the `resolve_to_addrs` pinning behaviour end-to-end against a `wiremock` mock server.

## Verification
- [x] `cargo test -p sera-runtime --lib` — 542 passed
- [x] `cargo clippy -p sera-runtime --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace -- -D warnings` — clean

## Test plan
- [ ] Confirm production deployments configure `SERA_CORE_URL` with a non-blocked host (the validator now treats loopback / RFC-1918 / cloud-metadata overrides as fatal — same as `http_request`).
- [ ] Smoke `spawn-ephemeral`, `knowledge-store`, `knowledge-query`, `tool-search`, `skill-search` against a real `sera-core` to confirm the pinned client still completes the request path.

author: m0a
body:
## Summary

Several CC Hub features were silently broken on macOS while working fine on Linux. This PR addresses three of them and bundles a Dashboard usage-limits UX improvement that surfaced during the same investigation.

## What was wrong

**Session list status indicator stayed on `completed` while Claude was running.**
Hook configuration was only checked for "any `cchub notify` entry exists", so a setup with only `Stop` + `PostToolUse(AskUserQuestion)` reported `configured=true` even though `PreToolUse` and `UserPromptSubmit` (the events that flip the indicator to `processing`) were missing. The setup banner never showed and users had no way to discover the gap.

**`/recap` output never appeared in the session list.**
Two bugs stacked:
1. `readLastLines` estimated 200 bytes per JSONL line, but Claude Code logs average ~2KB/line because of embedded tool results — a 300-line request only captured ~28 lines, dropping recent recap entries entirely.
2. `readLastAwaySummary` only matched `subtype:'away_summary'` (the auto-recap fired after 3min idle) and ignored manual `/recap` slash command output (which is stored as `subtype:'local_command'`).

**`cchub status` crashed on macOS.**
The command unconditionally invoked `systemctl --user`, which doesn't exist on darwin. `cchub setup` already handled launchd vs systemd; `status` was just left behind.

**Dashboard couldn't find Anthropic OAuth credentials on macOS.**
Newer Claude Code versions store the token in macOS Keychain (`Claude Code-credentials`) instead of `~/.claude/.credentials.json`, so usage limits silently failed with no UI feedback.

## Changes

### `fix: session indicator and cchub status on macOS`
- `/api/notify/hook-status` now reports per-event configuration (`stop`, `preToolUse`, `userPromptSubmit`, `askUserQuestion`) and a `missing[]` list. The setup banner triggers whenever any required hook is missing.
- The setup prompt sent to Claude covers all four events and explicitly tells Claude to merge with existing hooks (e.g. `prompt-recorder.sh`) rather than overwrite.
- `readLastLines` starts at 2KB/line and retries with 4× larger chunks (8K → 32K) if it hasn't captured enough lines, falling back to a full-file read.
- `readLastAwaySummary` → `readLastRecap`: also captures manual `/recap` output by tracking when the most recent user entry contains `<command-name>/recap</command-name>` and treating the following `system/local_command` as a recap. The latest of `away_summary` and `/recap` wins.
- `cchub status` checks `platform()` and uses `launchctl list com.cchub.server` on darwin (parses PID and `LastExitStatus` from the plist output).

### `feat(dashboard): Anthropic usage limits UX`
- Classifies API failures (`rate-limited` / `no-credentials` / `unauthorized` / `fetch-failed` / `unknown`) and surfaces a specific message instead of "Usage data unavailable". Cached values still display with a "(showing cached value)" badge during backoff.
- Honors `Retry-After` on 429 (clamped to 5min..1h) instead of always 5min.
- Reads OAuth token from macOS Keychain when `~/.claude/.credentials.json` is missing.
- User-Agent reports `cchub/<version>` instead of impersonating `claude-code/2.0.32`.
- DashboardPanel widens at xl/2xl breakpoints so the new error rows don't truncate.

### `chore: ignore local prompt history`
- Removes `.claude-user-prompts/*.jsonl` from tracking and adds the directory plus `.playwright-mcp/` and root-level `*.png` debug screenshots to `.gitignore`.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run --filter backend lint` passes (pre-existing warnings unchanged)
- [x] Verified `/api/notify/hook-status` against three settings.json variants (PreToolUse missing / only Stop / wrong PostToolUse matcher) — `configured`, `events`, `missing` all correct
- [x] Confirmed `/recap` output now appears in `ccRecap` via `/api/sessions` after the `readLastLines` and `readLastRecap` fixes
- [x] `bun run src/index.ts status` on macOS prints "Service status: Running (PID …)" via launchctl
- [x] `cchub notify` CLI still works (exit 0)
- [ ] Manual: bring up dev frontend, simulate rate-limited Anthropic response, confirm error banner shows the expected localized message
- [ ] Manual: verify hook setup banner triggers when settings.json is missing one of the four required events

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: sandarutharushka
body:
## Summary

Addresses 10 audit fixes against `qwen-coding-agent`, primarily around shell safety, test infrastructure, and memory store concurrency.

### Critical / High
- **FIX 1** — `cat`/`type` allowlist replaced with `isSafeCatCommand` helper that rejects absolute, `~`-relative, and `..` paths so secrets like `cat /home/user/.ssh/id_rsa` and `cat /root/.aws/credentials` no longer slip through. `SYSTEM_PATH_PATTERN` extended with `/home`, `/root`, `/var`.
- **FIX 2** — Added BLOCKED entries for `kill -9 1`, SIGKILL to `0`/`-1`, `pkill -9`, `truncate -s 0`, and redirects to non-`/dev/null` device files. CAUTION-level `kill`/`pkill` now require approval. Existing `DANGEROUS` switch arm preserved as an alias for CAUTION.
- **FIX 3** — Vitest wired up: `npm test`, `npm run test:watch`, `npm run test:coverage`, plus `vitest.config.ts`. `shellSafety.test.ts` rewritten with `describe`/`it.each`/`expect`. All 47 cases pass (40 existing + 7 new).
- **FIX 4** — Streaming fallback in `agent/agents/base.agent.ts` now logs the underlying error before retrying with non-streaming.

### Medium
- **FIX 5** — Tool-call JSON parse failures are now surfaced to the LLM as a tool-role message with the parse error and raw input, instead of silently substituting `{}`.
- **FIX 6** — `/tmp/agent_diff_*` replaced with `path.join(tmpdir(), …)` for cross-platform safety.
- **FIX 7** — `proper-lockfile` integrated. New `withMemoryLock` wraps `addTask`, `updateTaskStatus`, `addNote`, `addDecision` so concurrent writers can't clobber `.agent/memory.json`.
- **FIX 8** — `agent/cli.ts` prints a non-blocking `QWEN_API_KEY not set` warning at startup; `config show` / `config check` still work without a key.

### Low
- **FIX 9** — Stale "strip file contents" comment removed from `writeContext`; the field never existed.
- **FIX 10** — `AgentMemory.tasks` entries now carry a UUID `id`. `addTask` returns it. `updateTaskStatus` matches by ID first, falling back to last-matching task string.

## Test plan
- [x] `npm run build` (tsc) — passes
- [x] `npm test` (vitest run) — 47/47 pass
- [ ] `npx tsx src/safety/shellSafety.test.ts` — no longer applicable; the file uses vitest's runtime API per FIX 3 and must be invoked through the vitest runner.

author: aliebiac
body:
### Motivation
- 在现有 React 页面中展示二维中国地图轮廓并支持鼠标拖动与滚轮缩放，同时保持现有页面风格并避免 3D 效果。 
- 由于在当前环境中无法通过 npm 安装 `echarts`（访问受限），因此采用 CDN 动态加载并远程拉取 GeoJSON 的方式以保证项目可运行。 

### Description
- 新增组件 `src/components/ChinaMap.jsx`，按需通过 CDN 加载 ECharts (`https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/echarts@5/dist/echarts.min.js`)，并从 `https://geo.datav.aliyun.com/areas_v3/bound/100000_full.json` 拉取中国 GeoJSON 后使用 `echarts.registerMap` 注册并渲染地图，地图配置中使用 `geo` + `roam: true` 开启拖拽与缩放交互。 
- 将首页原占位替换为 `ChinaMap`（修改文件 `src/App.jsx`），并在 `src/styles.css` 中新增/调整 `.china-map` 与 `.map-error` 的样式以保持与现有页面风格一致。 
- 组件实现了 tooltip、窗口 `resize` 自适应、错误展示和卸载时的清理逻辑以避免内存泄漏或重复监听。 

### Testing
- 尝试运行 `npm install echarts echarts-for-react` 返回 403（受仓库访问策略限制），因此采用 CDN 方案并未将 `echarts` 加入依赖，安装步骤失败。 
- 使用 `npm run build`（Vite）进行构建验证，构建成功（输出显示 `built`），用于确认代码与打包流程无错误。 
- 未运行额外的自动化单元测试；构建成功作为当前变更的主要自动化验证。

author: copilot
body:
The upstream OpenAPI spec for `/openai/images/generations` and `/openai/images/edits` replaced the fixed `size` enum with a free-form string accepting any `WIDTHxHEIGHT` pattern, and changed the generations default from `1024x1024` to `auto`. The MCP server's Literal types and hardcoded default were out of sync.

## Changes

- **`core/types.py`**: Replace `ImageSize` and `ImageEditSize` `Literal[...]` enums with `Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r'^(auto|\d+x\d+)$')]` to preserve runtime validation while accepting custom dimensions; update `DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE` from `"1024x1024"` → `"auto"`
- **`tools/image_tools.py`**: Update `size` parameter descriptions to document the `WIDTHxHEIGHT` pattern, gpt-image-2 custom size constraints (multiples of 16, ≤3840 longer side, ≤8.3MP), and per-model presets
- **`tools/info_tools.py`**: Update Supported Sizes table (`auto` as default, note on custom gpt-image-2 dimensions) and usage guide default

```python
# Before — only accepted predefined values
ImageSize = Literal["1024x1024", "1536x1024", ..., "auto"]  # 17 options
DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE: ImageSize = "1024x1024"

# After — accepts any valid WIDTHxHEIGHT string with pattern validation
ImageSize = Annotated[str, Field(pattern=r"^(auto|\d+x\d+)$")]
DEFAULT_IMAGE_SIZE: ImageSize = "auto"
```

author: yangbooom
body:
## Summary

walla-next [#946](https://github.com/teamPaprika/walla-next/pull/946) 의 `_local_runner.yml` 패턴을 walla-docs 의 두 워크플로우에 미러. GitHub Actions 무료 분(分) 한도 절감 + chuncom self-hosted runner 동작 검증 목적.

> **Draft 상태:** PR 생성 자체가 \`preview_local_runner.yml\` 1차 검증. chuncom 에 walla-docs 가 등록되어 있고 Node 22 + pnpm 환경이 갖춰진 상태에서 빌드가 도는지 actions 결과로 확인.

## Pattern

| 기존 (비활성) | 새 (chuncom) | 트리거 |
|---|---|---|
| \`deploy.yml\` | \`deploy_local_runner.yml\` | main push + workflow_dispatch |
| \`preview.yml\` | \`preview_local_runner.yml\` | pull_request + workflow_dispatch |

기존 yml 은 보존 (\`on:\` 자동 트리거 주석화 + \`workflow_dispatch\` fallback 유지). 부활 시 주석 해제만으로 즉시 원복.

## chuncom 공통 설정

- \`runs-on: [self-hosted, Windows, X64]\`
- \`defaults.run.shell: 'C:\\PROGRA~1\\Git\\bin\\bash.exe --noprofile --norc -eo pipefail {0}'\` — Git Bash 8.3 short path 명시 (공백 회피, WSL bash 회피)
- 별도 concurrency group (\`pages-local-runner\`, \`preview-local-runner-...\`)
- Node 22 + pnpm 흐름은 기존 yml 그대로

## 차이점 (vs walla-next #946)

| 항목 | walla-next | walla-docs |
|---|---|---|
| Docker buildx | dashboard/form 사용 | **사용 안 함** (단순 pnpm build → static export) |
| 검증 브랜치를 deploy 트리거에 포함 | dev 환경이라 포함 | **포함 안 함** — Pages 가 main source 전제. PR 단계 검증은 \`preview_local_runner.yml\` 에 위임 |

## 사전 확인 필요 사항

- [ ] chuncom runner 가 walla-docs 리포에서 사용 가능한지 (org-level 등록인지 repo-level 인지)
- [ ] chuncom 호스트에 Node 22 + pnpm 설치 (또는 \`actions/setup-node\` 가 자동 설치 처리하는지)
- [ ] \`actions/upload-pages-artifact@v3\` + \`actions/deploy-pages@v4\` 가 self-hosted Windows 에서 동작하는지 (PR 머지 후 main push 로 검증)

## Test plan

- [ ] 이 PR 생성 → \`PR Preview Build (local runner)\` 가 chuncom 에서 빌드 성공하는지 actions 결과 확인
- [ ] \`PR Preview Build\` (기존, GitHub-hosted) 는 트리거되지 않아야 함
- [ ] PR 머지 후 main push 로 \`Deploy to GitHub Pages (local runner)\` 가 chuncom 에서 빌드 + Pages 배포 성공하는지
- [ ] 1주 후 GitHub billing 분(分) 사용량 변화 확인 (이전 대비 walla-docs 빌드 분 0)

## 부활 절차

각 yml 의 비활성화 주석 블록 (\`# push:\` / \`# pull_request:\`) 을 주석 해제 + \`_local_runner.yml\` 의 동일 트리거 제거.

## 범위 외 (후속)

- chuncom 가용성 모니터링 (walla-next 와 공유)
- walla-next #946 머지 전이라면 self-hosted runner 등록 작업 동기화 필요

## Summary
Major security overhaul + roles system + audit trail. Fixes 13 new bugs (3 critical, 3 high, 7 medium) discovered during deep code review.

**Critical Fixes:**
- Token authentication middleware on ALL API endpoints (was completely unauthenticated)
- Rate limiting on login (5 attempts/15min per IP)
- Body size limit 10MB (DoS protection)

**Security Fixes:**
- 2FA disable now requires TOTP code (not just password)
- XSS sanitization in canjear codigo and 2FA display
- SW cache invalidation (v3 - never caches panel.html)

- Memory leak in messages.update event listeners (cleanup on both branches)
- Race condition in envioPersonalActivo (returns descriptive error)
- grupoUltimaActividad persisted to DB (survives restarts)
- Seller invites uses calendar period (start of week/month, not sliding window)
- Timezone fix in getSellerInvitesCount (uses Peru timezone)
- Reconnection lock prevents parallel reconnection storms
- Auto-cleanup of recovery codes, expired sessions, old login attempts

- Roles: Admin(full) > Seller(all except admin panel) > Client with membership(all features) > Client without membership(blocked)
- Audit log: tracks logins, 2FA changes with IP. Admin-only section in panel.

author: copilot
body:
The OpenAPI spec for `openai` changed the `size` field on both `/openai/images/generations` and `/openai/images/edits` from a closed enum of 18 preset values to a free-form string matching `^(auto|\d+x\d+)$`, enabling custom dimensions beyond the old presets.

## Changes

- **`openai/openai_cli/commands/image.py`**
  - Replaced `click.Choice([...])` on `--size` in both `image` and `edit` commands with a plain string option
  - Added `_validate_size()` callback enforcing the OpenAPI pattern `^(auto|\d+x\d+)$`, so invalid inputs are rejected at the CLI layer before hitting the API

```python
# Before: only allowed 18 hardcoded presets
--size [1024x1024|1792x1024|...|auto]

# After: any WIDTHxHEIGHT or 'auto'
--size 2560x1440   # now valid
--size 1254x1254   # 1K alias, now valid
--size bad_value   # rejected with clear error
```

author: lrh2000
body:
If a thread invokes `FairAttr::update` twice, there is no guarantee that `FairAttr::fetch_weight` will detect the second update. It may clear the `HAS_PENDING` bit based on the first update:
```
  [ Thread 1 ]                               [ Thread 2 ]

  pending_weight.store(100)
  weight.fetch_or(HAS_PENDING)
                                             weight.load() = HAS_PENDING
                                             pending_weight.load() = 100
  pending_weight.store(200)
  weight.fetch_or(HAS_PENDING)

                                             weight.compare_and_exchange(HAS_PENDING, 100) = Ok(())
```

I think using a spin lock to solve this race condition is unavoidable. However, we can keep the fast path lock-free. Therefore, there shouldn't be a performance penalty.

author: projectroadwatch-ph
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent title, icons, and card labels from overflowing or appearing too large on narrow screens.  
- Ensure both cards reliably fit side-by-side on small viewports by computing widths from the available space.  
- Provide consistent min/max sizes so the UI scales smoothly across device widths.

### Description
- Use `useWindowDimensions` to read viewport `width` and compute responsive values for typography and icons.  
- Calculate `cardWidth` from the viewport and horizontal padding and apply a fixed inter-card gap via `CARD_GAP`.

author: jcast90
body:
## Summary

- New \`rly install\` command builds + installs the user-visible Relay surfaces (cli, tui, gui) so the installed copies match the source on disk. Defaults to all three; can target one (\`rly install gui\`).
- Persists \`~/.relay/installed.json\` with per-surface version + git SHA + install time so we can detect drift between installed bits and source.
- Adds a per-command startup nudge that prints a dim one-liner to stderr when any surface is behind source. Suppressed for install/help/version, \`--json\`/\`--quiet\`, non-TTY stderr, and \`RELAY_NO_UPDATE_NUDGE=1\`.
- Adds \`rly install --check\` (drift report + suggested next command, no build) and \`--force\` (rebuild even when current).

## Why

The current onboarding requires \`rly rebuild --all\` to update everything; without flags rebuild only does \`dist\`. Users who run \`rly rebuild\` and relaunch from \`/Applications\` get a stale GUI silently — when that GUI then fails to find a working \`node\`, the failure mode is opaque (\"node: not found\" from the pnpm shim, or \`ERR_UNKNOWN_BUILTIN_MODULE\` from a cached old node binary). \`rly install\` is the single verb that does the right thing by default and gives us a manifest other surfaces can use.

\`rly rebuild\` is unchanged and still serves as the "build only, don't install" verb. The new install command composes \`runRebuild\` rather than duplicating it.

## What's NOT in this PR

- In-app update banner in the GUI (will follow in a separate PR — uses the manifest written here).
- TUI footer nudge (separate PR — uses the same manifest).
- Code-signed Tauri auto-updater (deferred — needs Apple Developer ID, hosted release manifest, and signing in CI; only worth doing once we have outside users).

## Test plan

- [x] \`rly install --help\` renders help
- [x] \`rly install --check\` on a fresh machine reports no manifest, suggests \`rly install\`, exits 1
- [x] \`rly install cli\` rebuilds dist and stamps the manifest
- [x] Re-running \`rly install cli\` short-circuits with \`skipped — already at <ver>\`
- [x] \`rly install cli --force\` rebuilds anyway
- [x] \`rly install tui\` runs cargo + copies binary to \`~/.cargo/bin/relay-tui\` + stamps manifest
- [x] Stale manifest entry triggers nudge on a non-suppressed command (verified via \`script -q\` for TTY)
- [x] \`--json\`, \`--quiet\`, install/version/help commands suppress the nudge
- [x] Bogus target (\`rly install bogus\`) exits 2 with help text
- [x] \`pnpm build\` (tsc) clean

author: tmaeder
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to [PR #209](https://github.com/tmaeder/queer-guide-hub/pull/209). The translation cutover routes `translate-i18n-batch` rows into `ai_suggestions` with `proposed_value: { field, value }` + `current_value: { value }` + `locale: <target>` — but the SuggestionsTab rendered both sides as raw JSON, so reviewers had to mentally diff `{"value":"Pride march in Berlin"}` against `{"field":"title","value":"Pride-Marsch in Berlin"}` to spot translation issues. This PR adds a translation-aware row renderer that shows the actual text side-by-side.

## Changes

- **New `TranslationDiff` component** in `SuggestionsTab.tsx`. Renders translation rows with:
  - A header line: `<field> · source → <locale>` (e.g. `title · source → de`)
  - A two-column source/translation view with the actual text — `whitespace: pre-wrap` so multi-paragraph descriptions render naturally
  - **Defensive fallback to `PrettyJson` dual-pane** if `proposed_value` / `current_value` don't match the expected shape (older rows, hand-crafted rows, future schema changes won't break the page)
- **Row branch.** When `s.suggestion_type === 'translation'`, render `TranslationDiff`. All other types keep the original dual-`PrettyJson` view — no behaviour change for tag / synonym / cluster_membership / etc.
- **Intro copy updated.** The queue description now mentions `translate-i18n-batch` and lists `translation` among the auto-applied types (PR #209 added this — copy was stale).

## Out of scope

- **Value-only edit form** for translation rows. The Edit button still opens the JSON textarea; for translations the reviewer has to edit `{"field":"title","value":"..."}` rather than just the translated string. Fine for the rare reviewer override; future enhancement if usage is high.
- **Locale-name expansion.** The locale code is shown raw (`de`, `fr`, `es-MX`). A friendlier label (`de — German`) is a small addition but not required.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm run typecheck`
- [x] `npm test` — 249 files / 2197 tests pass
- [x] `npm run lint` — no errors on changed file
- [ ] **Browser verification not run.** The Playwright MCP server disconnected mid-session, so I couldn't drive the dev server to verify the rendered output. Reviewer should:
  - Open `/admin/search-intelligence?tab=suggestions&type=translation` after this lands
  - Confirm translation rows show `<field> · source → <locale>` header + side-by-side text
  - Confirm tag / synonym / cluster_membership rows still render as JSON dual-pane (no regression)
  - Confirm a translation row with malformed `proposed_value` (e.g. one of the legacy rows pre-PR-209) falls back to JSON view and doesn't error

## Risks

1. **Defensive fallback.** I wrote the fallback because in the current DB there are zero translation rows (PR #209 just merged) — once the cron runs we'll have real shapes. The fallback ensures a malformed row degrades to the old view rather than rendering nothing.
2. **No new dependencies.** Pure React/MUI, no behavior change to any other path.

## References

- PR #209 — translate-i18n-batch producer cutover (this PR closes its noted UI follow-up).
- `src/components/admin/search-intelligence/SuggestionsTab.tsx` — the only file changed.

3. watchlist drift 업데이트 금지 + isDataQuarantined
4. sizingTier BLOCKED
5. tradeAllowed=false
6. sizePct=0

`server/types/dataQuality.ts` SSOT — `DataQualityInfo` + `WaitReason` (DATA_HOLD/SIZING_BLOCKED 신규) + `shouldBlockTradingByDataQuality` 공통 게이트.

**1차 로그 098460 +221% 시뮬**:
```
[EntryEngine] DATA_HOLD: [entryEngine.extensionPct] sanity violation absPct=221% > 90%
[AutoTrade] 고영(098460) → WAIT / DATA_HOLD / DATA_HOLD_STALE_BASE_OR_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENT
[SizingTier] BLOCKED / DATA_QUARANTINE_STALE_BASE_OR_SPLIT_ADJUSTMENT
[WatchlistManager] drift update skipped: ...
```

## ADR-0118 — 매수 차단 사유 진단 + `/scan_blockers`

사용자 보고 *"FOMC 다음날 매수 0건"* 직접 대응. 운영자가 텔레그램 한 번에 차단 게이트 식별:

- `ScanCounters` 8 카운터 확장 (waitDataHold/preBreakout/gateFail/sizingBlocked/driftRemove/driftCorpAction/volumeDrop/other)
- `ScanSummary.waitDistribution` + `macroGateState` 옵셔널 영속
- `formatScanBlockersMessage` SSOT — 진단 추정 11분기 (emergencyStop / autoTradeEnabled / sellOnlyMode / R6_DEFENSE / DATA_HOLD 30%+ / Gate 미달 50%+ 등)
- `/scan_blockers` 텔레그램 명령 (alias `/blockers`, `/why_no_buy`)
- `perSymbolEvaluation` 6 분기 wiring

```
📊 [매수 차단 사유 분포] 직전 스캔 (12:34 KST)
🛑 거시 게이트:
  • emergencyStop: off
  • 레짐: R4_NEUTRAL (Kelly ×0.50)
  • FOMC: POST_1 (Kelly ×1.30) → 결합 ×1.30
  • SELL_ONLY: ON ⚠️
📋 종목별 차단 (43개 후보):
  • 진입: 0개
  • Gate 재검증 미달: 25개
  • Pre-breakout WAIT: 7개
💡 추정 원인: SELL_ONLY 시간대 — 점심(12~13) 또는 장외.
```

## ENV 롤백 5종

| ENV | Default |
|-----|---------|
| `ENTRY_PRICE_AUTO_CORRECT_DISABLED` | **true** (정책, ADR-0115) |
| `PRE_BREAKOUT_FAILCOUNT_DISABLED` | **true** (정책, ADR-0115) |
| `EXECUTION_RELAXATION_ENABLED` | **false** (ADR-0116 wiring) |
| `DRIFT_INVALID_UNIVERSE_EXCLUDE` | **true** |
| `DATA_QUALITY_STRICT_DISABLED` | **false** (strict 활성, ADR-0117) |

author: fxprunayre
body:
DCAT-AP plugin expect a specific structure of the RDF XML document as input. Here we check that this structure is as expected and reorganize the elements if necessary.

For example, we know that ISO formatter generate particular encoding that needs adaptation:
  * Does not describe catalog.
  * all `rdf:Description` elements are used instead of the specific DCAT classes (e.g. dcat:Dataset, dcat:CatalogRecord, etc.)
  eg.
  ```
  <rdf:Description ...
    <rdf:type rdf:resource="http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Dataset"/>
  ```
  should be converted to
  ```
  <dcat:Dataset ...
  ```
  * The main classes should be organized as follows:
  ```
  <rdf:RDF> MUST contain a dcat:Catalog
    <dcat:Catalog> MUST contain dcat:record, dcat:dataset, dcat:service elements
      <dcat:record>
      <dcat:dataset>
      <dcat:service>
  ```
  * Avoid having multiple reference to CatalogRecord with isPrimaryTopicOf.


The conversion can be applied on import for now. It is not automatic as we don't really have options to apply when a DCAT record is detected.


Topics to discuss:
* `dct:subject` are created when `Anchor` are used. Not supported in the editor
* Add support for `dct:accrualPeriodicity[dct:Frequency]`
* ...

author: copilot
body:
LLM model-selection decisions were scattered across route handlers, feature paths, and fallback calls — all reaching directly into `core.multi_llm_router.get_llm_router()`, mixing routing intent with provider supply execution and leaving no single place where routing truth lived.

## New canonical authority: `core/llm/route_authority.py`

- `LLMRouteAuthority` — single gate all LLM routing must pass through; `resolve()` produces a `LLMRouteDecision` before any provider execution occurs
- `LLMRouteRequest` / `LLMRouteDecision` — explicit input/output contracts with `LLM_ROUTE_AUTHORITY` sentinel embedded in every decision
- `get_llm_route_authority()` — singleton factory; callers use `.execution_router` to reach `MultiLLMRouter` for supply execution only

```python
# Before (routing decision implicit inside provider call)
from core.multi_llm_router import get_llm_router
llm_router = get_llm_router()

# After (routing authority is explicit; supply execution is delegated)
from core.llm.route_authority import get_llm_route_authority
llm_router = get_llm_route_authority().execution_router
```

## Callers updated to route through the authority

`core/routes/ai.py`, `core/routes/nodes.py`, `core/routes/system.py`, `core/routes/observability.py`, `core/system_integration.py` — all replaced direct `get_llm_router()` calls with `get_llm_route_authority().execution_router`.

## Legacy path registry (`core/orchestration_authority/legacy_paths.py`)

12 PR-L1 entries added — 7 updated paths (audit trail of pre-L1 bypass state) + 5 remaining callers (`openclawd`, `agent/kernel`, `ai_intent`, `galaxy_orchestrator`, `dashboard`) flagged `LEGACY_COMPATIBILITY` for migration in a follow-on PR.

## Package re-exports (`core/llm/__init__.py`)

`LLM_ROUTE_AUTHORITY`, `LLMRouteAuthority`, `LLMRouteRequest`, `LLMRouteDecision`, and `get_llm_route_authority` re-exported alongside existing `MultiLLMRouter` compat symbols.

## Docs

`docs/MODEL_ROUTING_AUTHORITY.md` §9 added: authority/supply separation rationale, canonical data flow diagram, list of updated and remaining callers.

## Tests

`tests/test_l1_llm_routing_authority.py` — 66 new tests covering sentinel importability, `LLMRouteRequest` field constraints, `LLMRouteDecision` invariants (authority always equals sentinel), `resolve()` contracts, package re-exports, all 12 legacy registry entries, and doc content assertions. All 126 routing-authority tests pass (60 existing PR53 + 66 new).

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

## Objective
Unify LLM routing under a single router authority in `DannyFish-11/ufo-galaxy-realization-v2`, so all model-selection decisions are derived from one canonical routing layer instead of being split across provider-specific paths, feature-specific branches, or compatibility fallbacks.

## Why this change is needed
As the system grows, LLM routing logic often drifts into multiple places: feature handlers choose models directly, provider-specific code quietly changes routing behavior, fallback paths become hidden route authorities, and compatibility shims preserve legacy model selection semantics. Even when each path works individually, the result is a fragmented routing reality where the system no longer has one authoritative answer to a simple question: "Which model should handle this cognitive task, and why?"

In the target architecture, routing authority must be separated from provider supply. The router decides the canonical target model or route intent based on task, prompt shape, policy, capability, and legality. The provider layer then attempts to satisfy that route according to availability, ordering, and fallback rules. If these concerns remain mixed together, provider code starts to act like routing authority, and different features silently acquire their own model-selection semantics.

## Required outcome
Implement a structural closure so all LLM model-selection decisions flow through one canonical router authority before reaching provider execution and supply resolution.

### Routing concerns to unify
At minimum, audit and unify routing for:
- prompt type / task type to model route mapping
- feature-specific model selection branches
- mode-specific or capability-specific routing
- compatibility or legacy routing shims
- fallback paths that currently redefine routing intent
- direct provider/model selection outside the central router

### Mandatory behavior
- All cognitive / LLM requests must first resolve through one router authority.
- Provider-specific code must not act as de facto route authority.
- Feature-specific code must not directly define private routing semantics when a canonical router decision should exist.
- Compatibility and fallback behavior may adapt execution, but they must not bypass the canonical route decision.
- The code should make it obvious where routing truth lives.

## Constraints
- Do not solve this only with naming cleanup or a thin wrapper while preserving scattered routing logic underneath.
- Do not keep legacy direct-model-selection paths as hidden exceptions unless they still terminate in the canonical router decision.
- Preserve necessary provider integration behavior, but keep routing authority separate from supply execution.
- Favor one authoritative routing model over preserving feature-local routing convenience.

## Acceptance criteria
1. All LLM/model-selection decisions pass through a single router authority.
2. Provider-specific branches no longer act as hidden route owners.
3. Feature-specific and fallback paths do not bypass canonical routing intent.
4. Routing authority is clearly separated from provider supply and execution.
5. The resulting code prepares the repository for model-supply truth and fallback-legality unification.

## Notes
This PR starts the LLM/cognitive authority phase after completion, continuity, readiness, orchestration, and center-boundary closure. Favor changes that make later provider ordering, fallback legality, and cognitive input assembly work easier.

author: finettt
body:
Overhaul the shell execution security architecture from a simple blocklist to a comprehensive allowlist + ExecPolicy model:

- Add ExecPlan for normalised, SHA-256 hash-locked execution plans that prevent substitution attacks between approval and execution
- Add ExecPlanner with shell metacharacter rejection in DIRECT mode, trusted-directory-only exe resolution, and workspace cwd validation
- Add ExecPolicy with DENY/ALLOWLIST/FULL security levels and configurable ask modes (OFF/ON_MISS/ALWAYS)
- Add AllowlistEntry for fine-grained argv validation including flag allowlists, denied flags, inline-eval protection, and positional argument limits
- Fix path traversal sibling-directory bypass (MED-2) by using separator-terminated prefix in PathValidator
- Protect identity files (MED-1) from LLM-instructed overwrite via VFS PROTECTED_PATHS and OS-level read-only bit
- Add Python safe mode that injects __import__ hook blocking dangerous modules (os, subprocess, socket, etc.)
- Harden approval flow to show normalised ExecPlan description instead of raw LLM string (prevents prompt injection)
- Deny shell/python in background workers (CRIT-3) unless backgroundShellEnabled is explicitly set, with audit notifications
- Add backgroundShellEnabled and customAllowlist to AgentConfig
- Add "full" sandbox mode with mandatory approval
- Conditionally register tools based on sandbox mode

BREAKING CHANGE: ShellConfig API completely rewritten; raw-string execute() methods replaced with ExecPlan-based API

The open-PR chip in sm log was rendered with NeonLime, which is the
same colour used by both the CI-pass badge and the merge-ready
badge. Three greens in a row on a healthy row (#15 open / CI / ready)
made it impossible to tell at a glance which chip was carrying the
status signal — the eye couldn't tell that two of those greens are
status (the only ones the user should be reading colour off of) and
one is just decoration.

The literal word "open" already encodes PR state, so the colour on
that chip wasn't doing semantic work — it was just brand. Switching
it to NeonPink keeps the brand identity (NeonPink is already in the
title gradient) while parking "open" outside the success/warn/fail
colour vocabulary used by the CI and merge badges. The other state
colours (yellow=draft, purple=merged, dim=closed) keep doing real
work because the colour reinforces a meaningful state distinct from
the literal word.

Single-line palette change in internal/ui/theme/palette.go; every
consumer (theme.PROpen, sm log, sm show, sm submit's PR list) flows
through the RolePROpen alias automatically.

author: jztang-ship-it
body:
## Summary
- Fixes the UX collision where the "you're on the leaderboard" chad commentary and the Google sign-in / RegisterModal could render simultaneously after a hand resolves.
- Adds a synchronous ref-based mutex in shared `GameView.tsx`: while either is in flight, the other defers to the next IDLE re-evaluation. Lives in shared code so basketball + baseball + worldcup all inherit the fix.
- Preserves chad's intentional chained "leaderboard_intro → sign-up nudge" sequence (call goes through BEFORE the mutex flag is raised).

## Diagnosis (root cause)
- Chad commentary trigger: `shared/views/GameView.tsx:522` (lb_shown / leaderboard_intro), `:523` (big_win), fired via `setFtueCommentaryOverride` at `:535`.
- Auth modal trigger: three independent gates funnel through `tryOpenAuthModal` at `:488`:
  - chad's own follow-up at `:541` (delay 4500ms)
  - MVP/LEGEND big_win at `:549` (delay 2500ms)
  - hand_5 fallback at `:557` (delay 3500ms)
- Collision: at the same IDLE tick, the chad effect and a sibling auth-nudge effect both fire. The sibling's 2500ms timer pops `setShowRegisterModal(true)` while the sticky chad message is still displayed.
- `tryOpenAuthModal` only deduped against itself via `rm_auth_modal_shown`; nothing checked the chad commentary state.

## Fix
- New refs `chadCommentaryActiveRef` and `authModalPendingRef` (synchronous, ref-based — useEffect-synced state would be one tick stale relative to sibling effects on the same flush).
- `tryOpenAuthModal` early-returns when commentary is in flight, without burning `rm_auth_modal_shown` so a later IDLE can re-fire.
- Chad effect early-returns when auth modal is pending, without burning `rm_usher_*` so the same message can fire on a later IDLE.
- Mutex flags clear when their respective surfaces dismiss (override → null, modal → closed).

## Edge cases
- User signs in mid-flight: `isAnonymous` flips false → both anon-gated chad messages and auth-modal effects no-op. No drift.
- User dismisses modal without signing in: `rm_auth_modal_shown` stays "1" forever, so future `tryOpenAuthModal` calls bail at the first check. Chad messages flow normally on subsequent IDLEs.
- Chad's own chained 4500ms auth-modal call still goes through — call ordered before the mutex flag is raised.

## Verification
- `basketball/`, `baseball/`, `worldcup/` typechecks: all silent.
- Tests: 8 failed | 241 passed (matches baseline, no regression).
- No localStorage key migrations.

## Test plan
- [ ] Load basketball as anonymous, play hands until on leaderboard + handCount >= 5; verify only one of (chad message, auth modal) shows at a time.
- [ ] Same on baseball.
- [ ] Confirm chad's intentional "leaderboard_intro → 4500ms → sign-up modal" sequence still chains correctly when no sibling collision exists.
- [ ] Dismiss the auth modal without signing in; verify chad commentary still fires on the next IDLE if its condition holds.

This commit prepares for sm log --json / --porcelain (next commit on
the stack) without changing any user-visible behaviour. The default
sm log output is byte-identical to before.

What changed:

* New unexported types logData and logBranchNode capture the
  intermediate shape Log had been computing and rendering inline.
  logData carries trunk, current branch, and a recursive tree of
  branch nodes; each node carries its stack.Branch, a NeedsRestack
  flag, an optional *gh.PR, an optional *gh.PRStatus, and its
  children. Pointer-typed PR/Status preserves the "we know there's
  no value" vs "we never fetched" distinction the renderer already
  relied on.
* Service.Log is now a 4-line orchestrator: buildLogData → render.
* Service.buildLogData is the single seam where I/O happens — repo
  preflight, trunk lookup, stack.Load, current-branch read, optional
  gh PR + status fetches, and a one-shot computeNeedsRestackMap walk
  that batches every rev-parse upfront. The renderer is now pure.
* buildLogTree is the pure shape-builder pulled out of buildLogData
  so unit tests can pin the tree shape without a live git fixture.
* renderLogTree replaces the old renderNode-with-Service entry point.
  It consumes a *logData, takes no Service receiver, and produces
  the same banner + tree string Log used to build inline. renderNode
  drops to a free function with no receiver.
* computeNeedsRestackMap reuses the existing per-branch needsRestack
  helper so nav.go's lone caller keeps the same semantics; the
  helper itself didn't move.

Why this seam matters: with logData as the contract, the next commit
can add Service.LogData (public) returning a *LogResult that wraps
the same data plus BranchView mappings, then thread three formatters
(renderLogTree, renderLogJSON, renderLogPorcelain) off the same
intermediate. No ad-hoc fetch logic in any of them.

Tests added:

* TestBuildLogTreePinsShape — two-root non-linear graph; locks down
  root ordering and child wiring.
* TestBuildLogTreeWiresPRAndStatus — populates the PR / Status
  pointers from the input maps; nil when no entry; needsRestack map
  drives the per-node flag; pre-existing tree shape preserved.
* TestBuildLogTreeEmptyGraph — empty graph returns an empty (non-nil)
  slice so the renderer's "no tracked branches" hint can read it
  uniformly.
* TestRenderLogTreeContainsExpectedTokens — characterises the
  rendered output: banner, trunk header, every branch name, current
  marker, PR pills, needs-restack tag, last-child connector.
* TestRenderLogTreeEmptyGraphHint — pins the freshly-cloned-repo
  onboarding hint.

The two pre-existing renderCheckBadge / renderMergeBadge tests
continue to pass without modification.

go test ./... is green; go vet ./... is clean; gofmt -l reports no
diff. Default sm log against this repo's stack produces byte-
identical output to the pre-refactor binary.

author: copilot
body:
`GET /api` on the Management endpoint (port 4848) returned web-mounted APIs instead of management-mounted ones, because `ApiIndexHandler` hardcoded the mount filter to `"web"` regardless of the inbound connector.

## Changes

- **`ApiIndexHandler`**: Pass `WebRequest` into `getApiResources()` and derive the mount filter from the connector attribute (`CONNECTOR_ATTRIBUTE`) on the raw request — `"management"` for `API_CONNECTOR`, `"web"` otherwise (preserving existing behaviour for null/unknown connectors). This mirrors the logic already used in `SlashApiHandler.verifyRequestMounted()`.

```java
// Before
.filter(apiDescriptor -> apiDescriptor.getMount().contains("web"))

// After
final String connector = webRequest.getRawRequest() != null
    ? (String) webRequest.getRawRequest().getAttribute(DispatchConstants.CONNECTOR_ATTRIBUTE)
    : null;
final String mountFilter = DispatchConstants.API_CONNECTOR.equals(connector) ? "management" : "web";
.filter(apiDescriptor -> apiDescriptor.getMount().contains(mountFilter))
```

- **`ApiIndexHandlerTest`**: Added `testDoHandle_managementConnector()` to assert that requests arriving on `API_CONNECTOR` return only management-mounted APIs.

author: mikecranesync
body:
## Summary

Two of the daily-cron agents have been pushing error alerts into Telegram every run. Both root causes are trivial and independent:

### 1. Telegram HTTP 400 swallowing alerts (`lead_scout`, `asset_intel`)

`orchestrator._send_telegram()` always uses `parse_mode=Markdown`. When an agent's result dict contains a value with an unbalanced `_`, `*`, or `[]` (a region name like `north_america`, or a model number containing `_`), Telegram returns 400 "can't parse entities" and the alert is dropped to the log. We see exactly this in `lead_scout.log` and `asset_intel.log` (single line: `Telegram send failed: HTTP Error 400: Bad Request`).

**Fix:** on HTTP 400, retry once with no `parse_mode`. Markdown rendering is nice-to-have; delivery isn't. Also collapsed the bespoke send block in `run_daily_digest()` to share the same helper, so the digest gets the same fallback.

### 2. Atlas DNS failure (`cmms_sync`, `pm_escalation`)

Both scripts read `ATLAS_API_URL` from Doppler, which is `http://cmms-backend:8080` (Docker DNS name) — for in-container callers. Cron runs on the host, where that name doesn't resolve. Every run fails:

```
httpx.ConnectError: [Errno -3] Temporary failure in name resolution
```

**Fix:** read a new `ATLAS_API_HOST_URL` env var first, default to `http://localhost:8082` (the actual published host port — confirmed via `docker port cmms-backend` and a `curl localhost:8082` that returned 403 "auth required", proving the service is up). Container callers' use of `ATLAS_API_URL` is untouched.

## Out of scope (surfaced separately to Mike)

- `kb_growth` Docling 504 on PowerFlex-525 — `DOCLING_SERVE_MAX_SYNC_WAIT=600` is already applied but a 4.5 MB PDF still times out. Needs different fix (chunked retry tuning) — flagged.
- `morning_brief` `ModuleNotFoundError` — historical; commit `fcf878c` already fixed the import. Next 09:00 UTC cron will confirm.
- `mira-pipeline` Ollama embed failures — Bravo Mac Mini at `100.86.236.11:11434` is unreachable. Not an agent issue; ops/host problem.
- `mira-web` Resend 429 + missing `blog_drafts` table — separate from the agent system.

## Test plan

- [x] `python3 -c "import ast; ast.parse(...)"` on all three files — clean
- [ ] After merge + VPS pull, next cron runs (CMMS sync 16:00 ET / 20:00 UTC, PM escalation 22:00 ET / 02:00 UTC) — expect green tracebacks gone
- [ ] Verify lead_scout/asset_intel send a real Telegram message (instead of failing 400) on next 10:00 ET / 18:00 ET runs

body:
<!-- stac-man:stack-start -->
**Stack** _(managed by [stac-man](https://github.com/bluegardenproject/stac-man))_

- **#20 feat/log-json-porcelain ← this PR**
- #21 chore/cursor-caveman-mode
- #22 feat/progress-spinner
- #23 feat/sync-progress
<!-- stac-man:stack-end -->

Builds on the logData / renderLogTree seam from the previous commit
to give sm log two machine-readable output formats. The default
synthwave tree is unchanged.

What ships:

* New public types Service.LogResult and Service.LogBranch produced
  by Service.LogData(). Trunk is reported once at the top level;
  the Branches slice contains only tracked (non-trunk) branches in
  depth-first pre-order over name-sorted roots, so a parent always
  appears before its descendants and the same input graph always
  produces byte-identical output.
* Per-branch shape mirrors `sm show --json` so a single JSON parser
  handles both commands. The PRView struct (used by both) gains
  optional Checks (CheckRollup) and Mergeable (Mergeability) fields,
  populated by sm log when the gh round-trip provides them and left
  empty (omitempty) by sm show.
* New service.FormatLogPorcelain() emits one tab-separated row per
  tracked branch with no header. Empty fields are written as "-",
  booleans as "true" / "false". Column order is published as
  service.LogPorcelainColumns and is part of the stable contract:
  branch, parent, depth, pr_number, pr_state, ci, mergeable,
  is_current, needs_restack.
* cmd/log.go gains --json and --porcelain flags (mutually exclusive).
  Both honour the existing --no-pr / --no-checks / --no-merge-status
  opt-outs — the same options that suppress a badge in the rendered
  tree leave the equivalent JSON / porcelain field empty.

Why this shape: the roadmap called out "structured output for AI
agents and external tooling" and "use the same BranchView struct
for consistency". Sharing PRView (and matching field names on
LogBranch) means agents write one parser. The trunk-once-at-top
shape avoids the awkward redundant-trunk-row most CLIs end up with.
The pr-omitempty and checks/mergeable-omitempty rules let consumers
distinguish "no PR" from "PR present but field not computed".

Tests added:

* TestLogResultFromDataShape — pins trunk / current placement, root
  ordering, depth values, IsCurrent on the right row, child-name
  wiring, full PR mapping including checks + mergeable.
* TestLogResultFromDataRecordedPRWithoutLiveData — covers --no-pr:
  recorded PR number surfaces alone so consumers still see the link.
* TestFormatLogPorcelainSchema — pins column count, ordering, the
  dash-for-empty rule, true/false bool words, and exact byte output
  for three rows covering open / draft+failing+conflict / no-PR.
* TestFormatLogPorcelainEmpty — empty graph emits zero rows
  (porcelain stays silent so scripts don't see schema-corrupting
  hint lines).
* TestPorcelainPRStateVocab — locks open / draft / merged / closed
  vocabulary so it stays in lock-step with the rendered tree pills.

Docs updated:

* docs/site/commands/log.md gains --json / --porcelain in the
  synopsis + flags table, and a full Scripting section with the
  JSON shape, jq recipes, the porcelain column table, and a sample
  pipeline.
* docs/skills/stac-man/SKILL.md updates the sm log row to mention
  the new flags and rewrites the "reading branch state
  programmatically" guidance to point at sm log --json for stack-
  wide queries (sm show --json stays the per-branch path).

go test ./... is green; gofmt -l is clean; go vet ./... is clean.
Smoke-tested live against this repo's stack: --json round-trips
through `jq`, --porcelain parses correctly with `cut` and `awk`.

author: thukumo
body:
Cloudflare WARP uses fwmark for policy-based routing, which causes packets to be dropped by the kernel when strict reverse path filtering (rp_filter = 1) is enabled (the default in NixOS).

This commit sets `net.ipv4.conf.all.src_valid_mark = 1` when the module is enabled. This instructs the kernel to consider fwmark during rp_filter validation, resolving the routing issue without needing to globally weaken the firewall to `checkReversePath = "loose"`.

Fixes #504119

author: clemisch
body:
Introduces model for sample-detector displacement, assuming transmission geometry and a flat detector as presented in [Hulbert2023](https://doi.org/10.1107/S1600576722011360).

Unlike other displacements (`m2ThetaDisplacement`, `m2ThetaTransparency`) which act only on the whole PowderPattern (i.e. all phases), this new displacement can act _also_ per-phase. In each `PowderPatternDiffraction` it combines per-sample and per-phase displacement and computes resulting 2θ shift from it. 

`m2ThetaFlatDetDispRatio` is the sample displacement, and `m2ThetaPhaseFlatDetDispRatio` is the per-phase displacement.

GSAS-II has something similar called `LayerDisp` [here](https://github.com/AdvancedPhotonSource/GSAS-II/blob/3daff4264639eb9cedc59665a7e9d83c446517fe/GSASII/GSASIIstrMath.py#L3523) which allows per-phase offsets. Afaik it's currently undocumented.

HermesCronBehavior flags (HERMES_CRON_SESSION, HERMES_CRON_AUTO_DELIVER_*) force `cron_mode=deny` in `check_all_command_guards`, which silently bypasses the blocking gateway/ask approval flow for dangerous commands.

body:
## Summary

Adds the PR301 deploy-validation tooling and fixes needed to run a realistic Duke IID startup-kit validation before merging PR301.

Changes include:
- Duke IID 3-site startup-kit project config for Cosmos server/admin plus `node_A`/`node_B`/`node_C` clients.
- Deploy smoke runner support for skipping built-in eval, selecting result directories, collecting checkpoints/logs, checking client logs, and cleaning stale NVFlare containers more aggressively.
- `dl0` post-training eval smoke script for Duke test and ODELIA challenge institutions.
- Local training live-monitor fixes: capture console output into `local_training_console_output.txt`, preserve training exit status, and keep final live sync behavior.
- Live-sync run selection fix so local monitor uploads the active startup-kit run instead of stale root-owned scratch artifacts.
- Startup-kit container robustness fix for PyTorch/NVFlare file descriptor pressure: raise Docker `nofile` to 65536 and set torch multiprocessing sharing strategy to `file_system`.

## Root Cause / Why

The PR301 validation hit two integration issues before the full run could complete:

1. Local training output was not reliably visible in the web live monitor because the startup-kit local-training path did not tee the training console into a startup-dir file that `live_sync.sh` could upload.
2. The 20-round MST swarm run failed near round 19 under the default Docker file descriptor limit. Persistent DataLoader workers and PyTorch multiprocessing shared-memory handles reached the default `nofile=1024` limit.

This branch fixes both issues and adds repeatable scripts/docs for the same validation workflow.

## Validation

Performed on the 3-node Duke IID infrastructure:

- Local monitor debug: MST `NUM_EPOCHS=1` ran on `dl0`, `dl2`, and `dl3`; console output, heartbeat/final heartbeat, and artifacts uploaded to `/srv/mediswarm/live`.
- Full startup-kit MST run on image `jefftud/odelia:1.4.3-dev.260429.8ac8f85` completed 20/20 rounds.
- MST job id: `7564b543-d4c9-4a3a-8a49-8b3afe891f63`.
- Final `FL_global_model.pt` collected from all three sites with identical md5: `43e4b0e92648a9c71a3223a019655681`.
- `dl0` eval smoke passed on Duke held-out test and ODELIA `CAM MHA RSH RUMC UKA UMCU`.

`1DivideAndConquer` was deliberately terminated at user request before the full 20-round run so we could inspect MST validation and performance first.

## Notes

The deploy-site config remains local-only and is ignored because it contains machine-specific paths and credentials.

body: The `len() >= capacity()` check on `cached_paths` evicted against the set's actual allocation rather than the `with_capacity(1000)` hint, so the bound moved with the set instead of holding it at 1000. author: nitishagar
body:
Closes #1394.

Adds a "Screenshot" button next to the Fullscreen button on the action bar. Captures the current WebRTC `<video>` frame via an offscreen canvas and downloads a PNG at the native stream resolution.

### Changes
- `ui/src/components/WebRTCVideo.tsx` — new `takeScreenshot` callback, wired to the existing `videoElm` ref; guards against unready streams (`videoWidth/videoHeight === 0`).
- `ui/src/components/ActionBar.tsx` — new `LuCamera` button inside the existing `lg:flex` wrapper, positioned immediately before the Fullscreen `SplitButtonGroup`.
- `ui/localization/messages/*.json` — new `action_bar_screenshot` key, machine-translated to every existing locale.

### Implementation notes
- Filename format: `JetKVM <W>x<H> <YYYY-MM-DD> at <HH.MM.SS>.png`, matching the reporter's proposal. Timestamp is built from local `Date` components (not `toISOString()`) so that a 6pm-local screenshot actually reads `18.00.00` instead of a UTC-shifted time that looks like a bug.
- Icon is `LuCamera` from `react-icons/lu` — no new dependency, visually consistent with the sibling icons (`LuMaximize`, `LuSettings`, etc.).
- The callback lives in `WebRTCVideo.tsx` and is passed down as a prop, mirroring the existing `requestFullscreen` plumbing through the same component interface.
- Button is gated behind the same `lg:flex` breakpoint wrapper as Fullscreen. Happy to surface it on smaller breakpoints if preferred.
- No CORS taint concern: the `<video>` is fed by a local WebRTC `MediaStream`, so `canvas.toDataURL` is safe.

### Testing
- `npm run lint:only`, `npm run build:device`, `npm run i18n:validate`, and `npm run i18n:find-unused` all pass locally.
- End-to-end device verification is pending — I don't currently have JetKVM hardware on hand. Reviewer verification on a live device would be appreciated.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

> **Low Risk**
> Low risk UI-only change that captures a client-side video frame to a downloaded PNG; main risk is minor UX/browser compatibility around canvas capture and download behavior.

> **Overview**
> Adds a new **Screenshot** control to the KVM `Actionbar`, wired from `WebRTCVideo` via a new `takeScreenshot` prop.

> The screenshot implementation captures the current WebRTC `<video>` frame into an offscreen canvas and triggers a PNG download with a timestamped filename, with guards for uninitialized video dimensions.
> 
> Updates i18n message catalogs to include the new `action_bar_screenshot` label across locales (and fills in additional missing Welsh strings related to advanced reset/network time sync).
