author: gmanfoofoo
body:
## TL;DR

Beide User-Bugs vom 2026-04-30 hatten dieselbe Ursache: ein versteckter `"use server"`-Export-Fehler in `inquiry.ts` ließ den Server-Action-Endpoint nie registrieren. Form-Submits liefen ins Leere → 404. Validation-Errors nie sichtbar weil die Action gar nicht startete.

Diese PR fixt das + bringt eine Playwright-E2E-Suite mit, die genau diesen Fehler in Zukunft sofort fängt.

## Root Cause

Next.js 15+ akzeptiert in einem `"use server"`-File **nur async functions** als Exports. `inquiry.ts` exportierte zusätzlich:
- `InquiryType` (type — wird von TS gestripped, OK)
- `InquiryState` (type — OK)
- `INQUIRY_INITIAL_STATE` (**const object — Bug**)

Module-Evaluation crasht mit:

> A "use server" file can only export async functions, found object.
> Read more: https://nextjs.org/docs/messages/invalid-use-server-value

Folge: Server-Action-Endpoint registriert nicht, jeder POST gegen `/kontakt` oder `/feiern` returnt 404. Form-State bleibt `idle`, also auch keine Validation-Errors sichtbar — beide User-Beobachtungen erklären sich aus diesem einen Crash.

## Fix

Neue Datei `src/app/actions/inquiry-state.ts` (kein `"use server"`) mit Types + Initial-State. `inquiry.ts` importiert die Types nur für Typing, exportiert ausschließlich die `sendInquiry` async function. ContactForm + FeiernForm importieren `INQUIRY_INITIAL_STATE` von der neuen Datei.

## Playwright-Suite (Commit 2)

`@playwright/test@1.59.1` + chromium. `playwright.config.ts` startet `next dev` auf Port 3002 mit gelöschten `SMTP_*`-ENVs → Server Action läuft im Dry-Run-Mode → keine echten Mails.

10 Tests, alle grün:

**`contact-form.spec.ts`:**
- Happy Path → Grazie-Panel
- Leere Submit → 3 field errors + Form-Summary
- Invalid Email → field error
- 500-Char-Name → server-side slicing, Success
- Honeypot (`website` gefüllt) → Silent Success ohne Leak

**`feiern-form.spec.ts`:**
- Happy Path → Grazie-Panel
- Leere Submit → 6 required-field errors
- Phone fehlt (Feiern-only required) → field error
- guestCount=0 → field error
- guestCount=\"viele\" → field error

Selectors via `input[name=\"...\"]` weil beide Pages einen `<section aria-labelledby=\"...\">` um die Form haben — `getByLabel` würde sowohl Section als auch Input matchen.

## npm scripts

\`\`\`bash
npm run test:e2e          # headless run
npm run test:e2e:ui       # interactive Playwright UI
npm run test:e2e:install  # one-time chromium download

## Summary

Hardens the QBO compliance scaffold (PRs #9, #10) against Intuit's published production review criteria. Targets specific items in their App Assessment questionnaire that the previous scaffold satisfied loosely or not at all.

## Gap matrix this PR closes

| Intuit requirement | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Privacy policy specifies QBO data read + retention + deletion-on-disconnect | ❌ generic | ✅ new section 5.1 |
| Privacy policy names sub-processors that touch QBO data | ❌ | ✅ Vercel, Infisical (both SOC 2) |
| Privacy policy commits to a deletion window | ❌ | ✅ 24h after disconnect notification |
| Integrations Terms — disclaimer of warranties | ⚠️ implicit | ✅ explicit section 6 |
| Integrations Terms — limitation of liability | ⚠️ implicit | ✅ explicit section 7 |
| Integrations Terms — termination + post-termination data flow | ⚠️ partial | ✅ explicit section 8 |
| Integrations Terms — governing law | ❌ | ✅ Dubai/UAE |
| Public support contact | 🔴 dead `/contact` link (404) | ✅ direct email/phone/address everywhere |
| Disconnect endpoint — audit log captures `intuit-tid` | ❌ | ✅ structured JSON per request |
| Disconnect endpoint — HMAC signature verification | ❌ | ✅ optional, env-gated by `QBO_WEBHOOK_VERIFIER_TOKEN` |

Items already shipped in PR #10 (HSTS, X-Frame, X-Content-Type, Referrer-Policy, Permissions-Policy via `next.config.ts`; OAuth `state` param; refresh-token rotation; minimum scope) confirmed compliant — no change needed.

## Out of scope for this PR (handled in mbr-brain)

- `qbo_client.py` switch from hardcoded endpoints to Intuit's OpenID discovery doc (C6)
- Capture of `intuit-tid` response header in client errors (H1, client-side)
- Exponential backoff on 429/5xx (J2)
- Operator `qbo purge` script — invoked when this endpoint logs a disconnect event, finishes the privacy-policy commitment within the 24h window

- [x] `npx eslint` clean
- [x] `npx next build` clean — all routes registered

body:
## UPDATED approach: on-demand revalidation

Switched from time-based (every 6h) to **on-demand revalidation**, triggered at the end of the daily LLM-matching cron (`/api/match-pending-stages`, runs 07:00 UTC after the three import crons at 06:00/06:15/06:30 UTC). The homepage is now fully static and rebuilt exactly once per day, right after all DB writes for the day are done.

### Changes
- `app/page.tsx`: removed `export const revalidate = 21600` — homepage back to default static behavior.
- `app/api/match-pending-stages/route.ts`: call `revalidatePath("/")` before returning. Done **unconditionally** (not gated on `success`): even if matching errors on some stages, the earlier import crons already mutated rows the homepage reads, so we want the page rebuilt regardless.

### Tradeoff
Manual DB edits via `/admin/*` won't surface on the homepage until the next 07:00 UTC cron run or a redeploy. Acceptable for now; if it becomes painful we can add `revalidatePath("/")` to the admin mutation handlers as a follow-up.

### How to test
- Deploy the branch.
- In Vercel → Cron Jobs, click **Run** on `match-pending-stages` to trigger it manually (or wait until 07:00 UTC).
- Make a small DB tweak (e.g. flip a `matching_result` row), re-run the cron, and confirm the homepage reflects the change within a few seconds without a redeploy.
- Function log should show `match-pending-stages: finished in ...`.

------ Old approach ------

## Note / open question
@technophile-04 I'm not totally sure this is the best approach. Instead, we could use **on-demand revalidation**, triggering it right at the end of the last daily cron job (currently `/api/import-tally-proposals/route.ts`, at least until we add the auto LLM-matching step).

The page would only refresh exactly when data changes, meaning no wasted regenerations. The tradeoff is that we'd have to call `revalidatePath("/")` from the cron route, and any manual DB edits wouldn't show up until the next daily run or a redeploy.

Happy to switch to this setup if you prefer it!

## Summary
Adds `export const revalidate = 21600` to `app/page.tsx` so the homepage dashboard regenerates every 6h instead of being served as static HTML from the last deploy. This ensures DB updates (manual edits, daily cron imports) actually surface to users without a redeploy.

## How to test
- Deploy the branch.
- Visit the homepage — should render normally.
- Make a DB edit (or wait for the daily cron). Within 6h the homepage should reflect it on the next request after the revalidation window expires.

body:
## Problem

`run-workers` has a hardcoded 10-min overall timeout (added in #5370). When it fires, all still-running workers are force-terminated and their results never reach the aggregated summary — silently dropped. No CLI/env/config override exists.

Hit this on a 4-worker run of a ~50-min sequential suite: only 28% of tests reported, with `[Main] Overall timeout reached (10 minutes)` at t=10m07s.

## Fix

Make the timeout configurable. Default `600000` ms preserved (backward-compat). Resolution order:

1. `CODECEPT_WORKERS_TIMEOUT` env var (ms)
2. `workersTimeout` in codecept.conf (ms)
3. Default `600000`

`0` disables the timeout entirely. Log message minutes value is now dynamic.

## Changes

- `lib/workers.js`: extract `_getWorkersTimeoutMs()`, gate `setTimeout` behind `> 0` check
- `typings/index.d.ts`: add `workersTimeout?: number` to `MainConfig`
- `test/unit/worker_test.js`: 6 unit tests (default / env / config / precedence / disabled / non-numeric fallback) — all pass

## Feature Epic: Tagging System UX Overhaul

Overhauls the tag input and display system across fanfiction.fyi with tokenized, auto-completing tag creation and categorized "chip" display on reading pages.

### 1. Creation UI: Enhanced TagChips Component

**Tokenization** — Pressing Enter, Tab, or `,` (comma) now immediately converts typed text into a visual chip/pill. Backspace removes the last chip when the input is empty.

**Keyboard Navigation** — Arrow Up/Down moves through the autocomplete dropdown. Enter or Tab selects the highlighted suggestion. Escape closes the dropdown.

**Highlighted Matches** — Matching substrings in suggestions are bolded in primary color for quick scanning.

**maxTags Prop** — Each tag type has a limit (Fandom: 5, Characters: 20, Relationships: 10, Additional Tags: 30). Input is disabled when the limit is reached, and a `{current}/{max}` counter shows in the label.

Groups tags by type in visual hierarchy order:

author: rman21
body:
## Summary
First of the Ch.1 boss-ability gaps from the diagnostic — **Pyredrake / Cinderblast**. Until now, Ch.1 Boss 1 ran only on the generic berserker enrage flag; the spec'd `CINDERBLAST` telegraphed row strike was unimplemented. The player therefore never saw a multi-turn telegraph until Ch.2's Hypnotist suggestions or Ch.3's Stormshepherd storms — three chapters in. This fix brings Ch.1 first-boss into Ch.2 archetype parity so the threat-banner pattern is taught at the door.

## Mechanic
- Every **6 turns** (P1) / **5** (P2) / **4** (P3) Pyredrake telegraphs a 4-cell row strike with a **2-turn timer**.
- Strike is **uncounterable** per spec — clearing the warning cells does NOT defuse. Player must absorb. Tradeoff: 2 turns of advance notice to stack shields or save ULTs.
- Damage tier scales by phase: **P1 = 1 tick**, **P2 = 2**, **P3 = 3**. Each tick = 1 shield (or 1 HP if shield-less), matching the Stormshepherd intensify cadence so players pattern-match instantly.

## Visuals (the \"визуальные эффекты\" Roman wanted)
- **Threat banner** — `⚠ CINDERBLAST in 2 turns — ember row incoming` shown for the full warning window via `showThreatBanner(text, 0)` (0 = persistent, clears on impact). Lives in the layout-stable banner slot landed yesterday → grid doesn't shift when the warning appears.
- **`.cell.cinderblast-warn`** — pulsing ember overlay on the 4 telegraphed cells. Radial gradient + ember border, 1.0s saturate breathing pulse (faster than the threat banner's 1.4s, so the eye reads it as \"more imminent\"). Cells stay playable during the warning — placement isn't blocked.
- **`.cell.cinderblast-hit`** — 0.55s strobe + scale burst at the moment of impact so the player can see exactly which row took the hit even if their gaze was on the boss bar.
- **Vibrate** patterns: `[60,40,80,40,100]` on warning queue, `[200,80,200,80,400]` on impact.
- **prefers-reduced-motion guard** on both cell classes.

## Implementation notes
- `_pyredrakeWarnCells: Set<\"r_c\">` is render-state — re-applied on every render() pass so the warn class survives grid rebuilds. Mirrors the existing chargedCells / radiantCells / _stormTimers convention.
- New `case 'berserker'` branch in `tickChapter2Archetype` gates on `currentBoss.id/name === 'pyredrake' / 'PYREDRAKE'` so future berserker bosses don't inherit this ability.
- `_resetPyredrakeState` wired into `startBossBattle`'s banner-clear block so Tower Pyredrake encounters reset clean.
- `render()` loop now stamps `data-row` / `data-col` on every cell — exposes what was already implicit (cell:nth-child math) so one-shot DOM operations (like the cinderblast-hit strobe) can target a specific cell without separate bookkeeping. Existing code paths unchanged.

## Test plan
- [ ] Vercel preview boots; play Ch.1 Boss 1 (Pyredrake)
- [ ] At turn 6 of P1: 4 cells in a random row glow ember + threat banner reads `⚠ CINDERBLAST in 2 turns — ember row incoming`
- [ ] During warning: cells stay playable (placement not blocked)
- [ ] At turn 8 (2 turns later): cells strobe red, banner clears, 1 shield (or 1 HP) consumed, `🔥 CINDERBLAST!` flash centered
- [ ] Phase 2 (≤66% HP): interval drops to 5 turns, damage = 2 ticks
- [ ] Phase 3 (≤33% HP): interval drops to 4 turns, damage = 3 ticks
- [ ] Battle reset (re-enter via Tower or replay): no leftover warning cells / banner
- [ ] No regression on the existing berserker enrage (×2 dmg at ≤50%) or attackInterval reduction
- [ ] Other Ch.1 bosses (Abyssal Tyrant etc., archetype != berserker OR id != pyredrake) do NOT trigger Cinderblast

body:
## Summary

- **WebSocket WAF reverse proxy** (`CfmsProxyHandler`): intercepts all client→CFMS frames, forwards CFMS→client unmodified; uses `CompletableFuture` to handle the race between `onOpen` and first incoming message
- **WafEngine**: Spring-managed rule list with hot enable/disable (no restart needed) via `ConcurrentHashMap`
- **5 detection rules**: SQL Injection, XSS, Path Traversal, Command Injection, Dangerous File Type (extension check on JSON frames + ELF/MZ magic-bytes check on binary chunks)
- **WafEventStore**: 500-event ring buffer, SSE real-time push to dashboard, atomic counters for stats, obfuscated log IDs (24-bit XOR from JWT secret SHA-256)
- **WafController REST API**: `/stats`, `/rules` (toggle), `/events`, `/events/stream` (SSE), `/events/export` (CSV)
- **Vulnerability demo endpoints** (all off by default via `application.properties`): JWT `alg:none` bypass, SSRF, reflected-CORS misconfiguration — used as attack targets in thesis demo

## Fixes in this PR

| Bug | Root cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `PathTraversalRule` / `CommandInjectionRule` / `FileTypeRule` defenseType shows as `HEUR/WAF.Generic.*` in dashboard | `name()` return values didn't match `WafEventStore` switch cases | Aligned rule names to `"… Detection"` pattern |
| `FileTypeRule` ELF/MZ magic-bytes detection never fires | `checkMagicBytes` checked offset 0 (frame_id bytes), not offset 5 (body) | Added `offset` param; binary chunks now inspected from frame-body start |

## Test plan

- [ ] Start Carapace, connect a CFMS client through the proxy
- [ ] Send a payload containing `' OR 1=1 --` → confirm 403 WAF block returned to client with correct `encryptedId`
- [ ] Upload a `.php` file → confirm blocked with `Dangerous file extension` reason
- [ ] Upload an ELF binary → confirm blocked with `ELF binary detected (magic bytes)`
- [ ] Open `/api/waf/stats` → verify counters increment
- [ ] Toggle a rule off via PUT, send matching payload → confirm it passes; toggle back → confirm blocked again
- [ ] Enable `vuln.jwt.alg-none.enabled=true`, send alg:none token → confirm accepted; disable → confirm rejected

### Issue for this PR

Closes #535

### Type of change

- [x] Refactor / code improvement

### What does this PR do?

Replaces `<div hidden={assistantCollapsed()}>` wrapping `AssistantParts` with `<Show when={assistantMessages().length > 0 && !assistantCollapsed()}>`. This causes SolidJS to truly destroy the entire component tree (Markdown renderers, tool calls, context groups) and all their reactive subscriptions when a turn is collapsed, instead of merely applying `display: none` CSS hiding.

The Markdown cache (200-entry global Map keyed by content hash) ensures completed messages re-render in ~5-10ms when re-expanded, since their content hasn't changed and the cache hit bypasses the full marked/shiki/katex parse pipeline.

### How did you verify your code works?

- `bun typecheck` passes across all 19 packages (ui, app, sdk, etc.)
- The change is minimal and scoped — only the `<Show>` condition and removal of the `hidden` attribute
- Existing `<Show when={!assistantCollapsed()}>` patterns for lighter elements (diffs, errors, thinking) are unchanged and already proven working

### Screenshots / recordings

Not applicable — this is an internal rendering optimization with no visible UI change.

author: pvliesdonk
body:
## Summary

Reverts the merge of #1585 (commit ff5478be).

The PR removed the alphabetical commit-/entry-beat heuristic from `interleave_cross_path_beats` and reframed Phase 4a's contract to permit multi-root output (R-4a.6). **That reframing is wrong.**

The right reading of the original problem (#1583):

> The alphabetical heuristic is wrong because it is *constraint-blind* — it can pick an ordering between concurrent dilemma commits that conflicts with explicit `wraps` / `serial` edges from SEED. The fix should produce *any* satisfying schedule consistent with all hard constraints, deterministically. A topological-sort-driven satisfaction primitive (which the codebase already has via `topological_sort_beats`) does exactly that, and naturally yields a single-rooted output.

What #1585 shipped instead:

> Removed the heuristic and accepted multi-root output as "by design" via R-4a.6 + new wording. That abdicates the satisfaction problem rather than solving it. The downstream stages (POLISH passage formation, R-7.2) still expect single-root input. Filing #1584 to defer the question pushed the band-aid one stage further down rather than fixing the actual algorithmic gap in GROW Phase 4a.

## What this revert restores

- `interleave_cross_path_beats` and `_build_hint_base_dag` and `detect_temporal_hint_conflicts` go back to their pre-#1585 shapes (alphabetical heuristic still present — broken in the same way it was before, but no worse).
- `check_single_root_beat` is re-wired into `run_grow_checks()`.
- Spec wording reverts: R-4a.6 is removed; R-3.1, R-4a.3, R-7.1, R-7.5, Stage Output Contract item 1 + 14, story-graph-ontology.md all revert to their pre-#1585 wording.
- Tests revert to their pre-#1585 assertions.

## Bookkeeping

- #1584 (the deferred POLISH single-start follow-up filed under the wrong premise) will be closed.
- #1583 (the original alphabetical-heuristic tracker) will be reopened so a proper constraint-aware satisfaction implementation can land.
- `projects/murder-haiku2` will once again hit the cycle halt at GROW Phase 4a until the proper fix lands. That is the intended state — the cycle halt is correctly identifying a real algorithmic gap, and #1585's fix masked the gap rather than addressing it.

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
closes #21734

Updates the zombie flow detection guide to use a `prefect.flow-run.*` wildcard in the automation's `expect` set instead of listing individual terminal state names (`Completed`, `Failed`, `Cancelled`, `Crashed`).

Flow run event names are based on the state's **name**, not its **type**. This means a flow finishing in a `COMPLETED` state with a custom name (e.g., `Completed(name="SuccessfullyProcessed")`) emits `prefect.flow-run.SuccessfullyProcessed`, which wouldn't match the previously documented `expect` set. Using the wildcard ensures the automation works correctly regardless of custom state names.

The wildcard approach is also simpler and more robust — any flow run event (heartbeat or state change) resets the proactive trigger timer, which is the correct behavior for zombie detection: if a flow is emitting any events at all, it's not a zombie.

Also adds a new "Custom state names" section that:
- Explains how flow run event names are derived from state names, not types
- Documents the alternative approach of explicitly listing custom state names in the `expect` set for finer-grained control
- Warns that missing names cause false-positive zombie detections

* 💡 **What:** Replaced dynamic threshold floating-point multiplications (`mouseDistance * mouseDistance` and `connectionDistance * connectionDistance`) with pre-calculated constant variables (`mouseDistanceSq` and `connectionDistanceSq`) outside the animation rendering loop. Also added the `.bundle` and `vendor` directories to `.gitignore` to maintain repository hygiene.

author: nicknisi
body: ## Summary Fixes #72 — `SyntaxError: eventemitter3 does not provide an export named 'default'` when any client route mounts `AuthKitProvider` in Vite dev. The root cause: client files statically import `actions.ts` / `server-functions.ts`, which statically import `auth-helpers.ts` → `authkit-loader.ts` → `@workos/authkit-session` → `@workos-inc/node`. Vite's dev server eagerly walks that graph, dragging the entire WorkOS Node SDK (and its `eventemitter3` CJS dep) into the browser bundle. ### What changed - **Lazy handler bodies**: each `createServerFn(...).handler(...)` is now a thin shell that `await import()`s its real logic from `action-bodies.ts` / `server-fn-bodies.ts`. The TanStack Start compiler rewrites these shells to `createClientRpc(id)` on the client side, so the dynamic import never fires in the browser. - **Type-only imports**: split three client-side co-imports of types + values (`AuthKitProvider.tsx`, `impersonation.tsx`, `types.ts`) so types are on separate `import type` lines. - **oxlint regression guard**: `.oxlintrc.json` now blocks static value imports of server-only modules in `actions.ts` / `server-functions.ts` (with `allowTypeImports: true`). - **Bundle-leak CI check**: `scripts/check-bundle-leak.sh` greps the example's built client bundle for server-side fingerprints (`@workos-inc/node`, `iron-session`, `FeatureFlagsRuntimeClient`, etc.). Wired into CI and `prepublishOnly`. - **CLAUDE.md**: documents the lazy-bodies pattern, load-bearing assumption (TanStack compiler must transform installed dist), and re-verification steps. ### Load-bearing assumption The fix relies on TanStack Start's compiler plugin transforming this SDK's installed `dist/**/*.js` files. The plugin's transform filter (`/\.[cm]?[tj]sx?($|\?)/`) has no `node_modules` exclusion as of `@tanstack/start-plugin-core@1.154.8`. Verified by inspecting the served module via `curl` against the example dev server — all 8 handler declarations are rewritten to `createClientRpc(id)` stubs with zero handler-body references remaining. If a future TanStack/Vite release changes this, `pnpm run build:check` will catch it. ## Test plan - [x] `pnpm typecheck` — passes - [x] `pnpm lint` — 0 warnings, 0 errors (oxlint guard active) - [x] `pnpm test` — 203 tests pass (17 files, no test modifications needed) - [x] `pnpm build` — passes - [x] `cd example && pnpm build` — no Node-only externalization warnings - [x] `pnpm run build:check` — no server-side fingerprints in client bundle - [x] Pre-flight verification: served `actions.js` and `server-functions.js` contain `createClientRpc` stubs, zero leaked handler-body refs - [x] Manual #72 repro: `cd example && pnpm dev` → load route with `AuthKitProvider` → **no eventemitter3 SyntaxError** - [x] Full auth flow: sign in → protected route → refresh → sign out — all working - [x] oxlint negative test: deliberate `import { getRawAuthFromContext } from './auth-helpers.js'` in `actions.ts` → lint fails with expected message - [x] oxlint positive test: `import type { AuthResult } from './auth-helpers.js'` → lint passes ---

author: bobpullie
body:
## Why — 위상군 (E:/DnT/DnT_WesangGoon) 인계, 5-Asset 4원칙 #4 Universal Portability 위반

### 재현
```bash
pip install git+https://github.com/bobpullie/TEMS.git
python -c "from tems.templates import preflight_hook"
# → FileNotFoundError: tems_agent_id not found from .../site-packages/tems/templates
```

### 본질

종전 ``find_agent_root`` 는 ``Path(__file__).resolve().parent`` 부터 ancestors marker walk. canonical pip install 시 ``start`` 가 ``.../site-packages/tems/templates`` 라 부모 어디에도 marker 없음 → ``raise FileNotFoundError`` → **module load 도 같이 raise** → ``from tems.templates import preflight_hook`` 자체가 fail.

PR #19 가 ``QMD_CMD`` 의 portability 결함을 정정한 것과 동일 카테고리 — 함수 다단 해상으로 일반화 + module load lazy 보장.

## What

### Layer 1 — find_agent_root 다단 해상 (위상군 처방)

```python
def find_agent_root(start: Path) -> Path:
    """env > cwd walk > __file__ walk > raise"""
    env = os.environ.get("TEMS_AGENT_ROOT")
    if env:
        root = Path(env).resolve()
        if (root / ".claude" / "tems_agent_id").exists():
            return root
        # env 박혔는데 marker 없으면 silent 하지 말고 즉시 raise
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"TEMS_AGENT_ROOT={env} but .claude/tems_agent_id not found there")

    for anchor in (Path.cwd(), start.resolve()):
        cur = anchor
        while cur != cur.parent:
            if (cur / ".claude" / "tems_agent_id").exists():
                return cur
            cur = cur.parent

    raise FileNotFoundError("tems_agent_id not found via TEMS_AGENT_ROOT env, cwd walk, or __file__ walk (start={start})")
```

해상 순서 근거:
1. **env** — site-packages canonical install 시 유일한 결정적 해법. 사용자 명시는 항상 자동 추론보다 우선
2. **cwd walk** — 현재 작업 중인 에이전트 프로젝트가 의도일 확률 최대 (CLI 호출 직관)
3. **__file__ walk** — v0.4 editable-in-project install 의 backward compat
4. env invalid 는 silent fallback 없이 즉시 raise — wrong-agent migration 방지

### Layer 2 — module load 강화 (카파시군)

위상군 처방의 1단계만 적용 시 함수가 5번째 안전망에서 raise → ``AGENT_ROOT = find_agent_root(...)`` module-level 호출도 같이 raise → ``import`` 자체 fail. 위상군이 진단한 본질 (import-only context) 가 해결되지 않음.

```python
def _resolve_agent_root():
    try:
        return find_agent_root(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return None  # module load 안전 — main() 시점에 재시도

AGENT_ROOT = _resolve_agent_root()  # Optional[Path]
AGENT_ID = (...)  if AGENT_ROOT is not None else None
DB_PATH = (...)   if AGENT_ROOT is not None else None
```

### Layer 3 — main() lazy retry

```python
def main():
    global AGENT_ROOT, AGENT_ID, DB_PATH
    if AGENT_ROOT is None:
        try:
            AGENT_ROOT = find_agent_root(Path(__file__).resolve().parent)
            AGENT_ID = ...
            DB_PATH = ...
        except FileNotFoundError:
            sys.exit(0)  # agent 환경 외부에서 hook 직접 실행 — config error
    ...
```

Hook execution context 의 cwd 는 보통 agent 안 — 그 시점에는 walk 성공.

### Layer 4 — _log_diagnostic AGENT_ROOT None safe

```python
def _log_diagnostic(event, exc):
    if AGENT_ROOT is None:
        return  # nowhere to persist
    ...
```

## Tests (신규 ``tests/test_find_agent_root.py``, 6건)

| Test | Assertion |
|------|-----------|
| ``test_find_agent_root_env_var_precedence`` | env 박힌 경로 최우선 (cwd / file 모두 무시) |
| ``test_find_agent_root_cwd_walk`` | env 부재 시 cwd 부터 위로 walk |
| ``test_find_agent_root_file_walk_fallback`` | cwd marker 밖일 때 __file__ 부터 walk (v0.4 backward compat) |
| ``test_find_agent_root_env_invalid_raises`` | env 박혔는데 marker 없으면 silent fallback 없이 즉시 raise |
| ``test_find_agent_root_site_packages_no_env`` | env 부재 + cwd / start 모두 marker 밖 → 명확한 raise |
| ``test_module_import_graceful_outside_agent_tree`` | **위상군 인계 본질** — site-packages 시뮬에서 ``importlib.reload`` 가 fail 없이 통과, AGENT_ROOT/AGENT_ID/DB_PATH 모두 None |

## Surgical scope

- ``preflight_hook.py`` 만 변경 (find_agent_root 정의 + module-level 변수 + main + _log_diagnostic)
- ``tems_commit.py``, ``tems_engine.py`` 등 다른 파일의 marker 해상 로직 (있다면) 동일 패턴으로 일반화는 별 PR 분리 권장 (현 PR surgical 유지)
- 호출 사이트 (AGENT_ID / DB_PATH 사용처 다수) 변경 0 — Optional 처리는 main() 진입 retry 로 일괄

## Regression

- ``pytest`` 전체: **75 passed** (이전 69 + 신규 6)
- 회귀 0

## Karpathy 4 원칙 self-check

| 원칙 | 적용 |
|------|------|
| 1. Think Before Coding | 위상군 처방 verify → 1단계만으로는 부족 (module load 까지 fail) 발견 → layer 2-4 강화 |
| 2. Simplicity First | helper 1개 (_resolve_agent_root) + None safe 처리. 추가 abstraction 0. |
| 3. Surgical Changes | preflight_hook.py 만 변경. 다른 marker 해상 코드 별 PR 분리. AGENT_ID/DB_PATH 호출 사이트 0 변경. |
| 4. Goal-Driven Execution | 6 test 가 5 시나리오 + import-only context 각각 독립 verify. 위상군 인계 본질 (import 통과) 마지막 test 가 직접 verify. |

## 위상군 인계 분류

| 인계 | 본 PR |

body:
## Summary
The privacy policy already discloses the affiliate-commission model in prose. But FTC + Amazon Associates both require disclosure **near the links themselves**, not buried in a policy page. This adds visible asides where affiliate links actually appear.

## Changes

### \`/guides/[slug]/links\`
Replaces the soft inline mention with an amber-bordered aside above the link list:

> **Affiliate disclosure**
> Some of the links on this page are **affiliate links**. If you click one and complete a purchase on the destination site, we may earn a commission at **no extra cost to you**. The price you pay is exactly the same as if you went to that site directly. Affiliate income is how we keep guide prices low and stay independent of any single tour operator.
>
> As an Amazon Associate, TestedRoutes earns from qualifying purchases.

The Amazon line is the canonical disclosure required by their operating agreement.

### \`/guides/[slug]\`
Adds a compact one-line variant of the same disclosure above the guide body, conditional on \`hasAffiliateLinks\`:

> **Affiliate disclosure.** Some links below are affiliate links – if you click and buy on the destination site, we may earn a commission at no extra cost to you. As an Amazon Associate, TestedRoutes earns from qualifying purchases. _More on how this works_

Currently \`hasAffiliateLinks\` is false on every published guide (no affiliate links embedded in body content yet). The aside hides automatically. The moment an editor adds the first affiliate link to a body block in Sanity (via the existing \`isAffiliate\` link annotation), the disclosure appears.

## Why this matters now
- Amazon Associates requires the canonical line near every Amazon link or your account can be terminated.
- FTC requires "clear and conspicuous" disclosure near the link, not in a footer policy.
- Awin, Impact, and most affiliate networks have similar contractual disclosure requirements.

author: lucos-developer[bot]
body:
Closes #238

`docker ps` (without `-a`) only lists running containers. If a container is stopped or exited, it still holds a reference to the volume, so `docker volume rm` fails with "volume is in use".

This fix adds a two-step approach:
1. Stop any running containers (unchanged behaviour)
2. Remove ALL containers referencing the volume (running, stopped, exited, created) before attempting the volume deletion

This ensures `docker volume rm` always succeeds regardless of container state.

author: angel-manuel
body:
## Summary

Adds the missing client-side OAuth path so Overslash can authenticate to upstream MCP servers (Overslash-as-MCP-client). Closes a one-click account-takeover vector: an attacker who steals an OAuth URL minted on their account cannot trick a victim into binding the victim's upstream tokens to the attacker's Overslash identity.

**Mechanism (single mechanism, opaque flow-id):**
- Base62 `flow_id` is the OAuth `state`. Trusted fields (initiating identity, PKCE verifier, AS endpoints, expiry) live in `mcp_upstream_flows`, never in the URL.
- `GET /gated-authorize?id=F` — fail-fast UX gate. Rejects clicks whose `oss_session` is not in the flow's identity tree, before the user types upstream credentials.
- `GET /oauth/upstream/callback?code=…&state=F` — re-enforces session-vs-flow before consuming the row and exchanging the code. **This is the security boundary.** Even with the raw upstream URL, a wrong-account session is refused.
- Tokens encrypted at rest (AES-256-GCM via existing secret-vault primitive); versioned per project convention.

**API surface:**
- `POST /v1/mcp_upstream/initiate` — RFC 9728 + RFC 8414 discovery, RFC 7591 DCR (public client only — confidential clients explicitly rejected), mint flow row, return `proxied` / `short` / `raw` URL forms. Idempotent: short-circuits with `status: ready` when a valid token exists; reuses an active flow row instead of churning fresh ones.
- `GET /gated-authorize` — the gate.
- `GET /oauth/upstream/callback` — the callback.
- `GET /v1/identities/{id}/mcp_upstream_connections` — list.
- `POST .../revoke` — revoke.

**Wiring:**
- `mcp_client.rs` surfaces `401 + WWW-Authenticate` as a structured `AuthRequired { resource_metadata_url }` error so callers can mint a flow.
- Best-effort `oversla.sh` short-URL minting via new `OVERSLA_SH_BASE_URL` / `OVERSLA_SH_API_KEY` config (unset → only proxied URL returned; never blocks the flow).
- Dashboard "Upstream MCP Connections" section on the agent page with initiate / revoke / status.

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo test -p overslash-api --test oauth_upstream` — 8 integration tests including the security-boundary test (`callback_rejects_when_session_doesnt_match_flow_security_boundary`)
- [x] `cargo test -p overslash-api --tests` — full integration suite green
- [x] 6 unit tests for the wire layer (PKCE, flow-id mint, authorize-URL builder, html_escape, WWW-Authenticate parser)
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --tests` — clean
- [x] `cargo sqlx prepare --workspace -- --tests` — offline cache regenerated and checked in
- [x] `make schema` — SCHEMA.sql refreshed
- [x] `npx svelte-check` — 0 errors, 0 warnings (476 files)
- [x] dashboard `vite build` — green (pre-commit hook)
- [ ] Manual end-to-end with a real upstream MCP server (staging)

author: owine
body:
## Summary

First production deploy of the GHCR image surfaced a real bug: the Dockerfile bakes a \`curl http://localhost:8080/healthz\` HEALTHCHECK that the worker and migrate containers inherit. The worker doesn't run an HTTP server, so the inherited check fails forever — Docker reports the worker as **unhealthy** and any \`depends_on: service_healthy\` chain in a deploy script (Watchtower, Portainer, custom scripts) gets stuck.

## Root cause

The Dockerfile's HEALTHCHECK was correct when the image's default CMD was \`python -m yas all\` (one container running everything). Compose splits services across distinct containers, where:

- \`yas-api\` → runs API server, healthcheck is correct (compose-overridden anyway)
- \`yas-worker\` → runs background loops, no HTTP. Inherits broken check.
- \`yas-migrate\` → one-shot alembic, exits in seconds. Inherits the check, reports unhealthy until it exits.

## Fix

\`\`\`yaml
yas-migrate:
  healthcheck:
    disable: true   # one-shot, exits before any meaningful check

yas-worker:
  healthcheck:
    disable: true   # no HTTP server
\`\`\`

The image contract is unchanged. Anyone running the image standalone with the default \`python -m yas all\` CMD still gets the baked HEALTHCHECK as a sensible default.

## Production deploy log (before fix)

\`\`\`
Container yas-migrate Exited
Container yas-worker Started
Container yas-api Healthy
container yas-worker is unhealthy
❌ Failed to deploy yas during deploy (timeout or error)
\`\`\`

The worker is *actually fine* — its logs show all loops starting cleanly:
\`\`\`
{"event": "worker.start", "level": "info"}
{"interval_s": 10, "event": "heartbeat.start"}
{"tick_s": 30, "event": "scheduler.start"}
{"tick_s": 60, "event": "delivery.start"}
{"event": "sweep.ran", "kids": 0}
{"event": "detector.ran", "stagnant_sites": 0}
{"event": "digest.ran", "kids": 0}
\`\`\`

It's just running with a misconfigured healthcheck.

## Test plan

- [x] \`docker compose config\` validates with both services showing \`healthcheck: disable: true\`
- [x] api keeps its explicit healthcheck (rendered output confirmed)
- [ ] CI passes
- [ ] Deploy host re-pulls and starts cleanly: \`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d\` no longer times out on worker

## Out of scope

- Removing HEALTHCHECK from the Dockerfile entirely. The current arrangement (sensible default + per-service overrides in compose) is the better split — anyone running the image with the default CMD still gets a working check.

## Summary by Sourcery

Disable inappropriate Dockerfile health checks for non-HTTP compose services to prevent false unhealthy states and deployment timeouts.

Bug Fixes:
- Disable the inherited Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK on the yas-migrate service so the one-shot migration container does not report as unhealthy before exiting.
- Disable the inherited Dockerfile HEALTHCHECK on the yas-worker service so the background worker is not permanently marked unhealthy and blocking depends_on health chains.

author: opencolin
body:
Previously, a 404 "Model not found" from the upstream provider returned
generic suggestions about checking the API key, permissions, and rate
limits — none of which were the actual problem. This was specifically
misleading when the proxy's bundled .env.example pinned a retired model:
the user's key and permissions were fine, the model just no longer
existed on their provider.

Now we pattern-match on the upstream error message and return suggestions
that match the failure mode:

- 404 / "not found"     -> point at BIG/MIDDLE/SMALL/VISION_MODEL config and
                           link to GET <base_url>/models for verification
- 401 / 403 / unauth    -> auth-key suggestions (the original default)
- 429 / "rate"          -> rate-limit suggestions
- anything else         -> the original generic three-line suggestion list

The error 'message' field still contains the raw upstream string, so the
existing diagnostic information is unchanged.

author: opencolin
body:
Boots the proxy in-process via Starlette's TestClient (no uvicorn, no
port binding), invokes /test-connection, prints the JSON result, and
exits 0 on success or 1 on failure. Intended for CI and install
scripts (install.sh inlines the equivalent boot+probe+kill logic today
and could be simplified to just call this).

We deliberately do not enter TestClient as a context manager, so
FastAPI lifespan handlers (which would open the observability sqlite
database and start a background recorder task) don't fire. /test-
connection itself records nothing, so this is sufficient for a clean
smoke test with no side effects.

author: opencolin
body:
4096 is below what Claude Code requests for many turns (especially
agentic tool-use loops), and reasoning-style Nebius models like
Kimi-K2.5, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, and Qwen3 thinking variants burn a
chunk of the budget on hidden reasoning before producing visible
output. Empirically a 64-token request to Kimi-K2.5 returns empty
text because the entire budget is consumed by reasoning; the default
should leave headroom for both that and Claude Code's own usage.

16k is a conservative middle ground. Provider-specific caps still
apply; users with tighter quotas can lower this.

## Summary
- add a fast path so `ElasticGraph::Support::Threading.parallel_map` uses normal `map` for exactly one item
- keep multi-item enumerables on the existing thread-per-item path
- add a benchmark plus captured results for the single-item fanout case

This avoids creating a Ruby thread for single-client msearch fanout, which is common for deployments that route queries through one datastore cluster.

`bundle exec ruby benchmarks/threading/parallel_map_single_item.rb`

- single entry hash: after path `3.23M i/s` vs before `27.6k i/s` (`117x` faster)
- `Thread.new` calls for 1,000 single-item maps: before `1000`, after `0`
- multi-item array: same-ish within benchmark error
- empty array: current implementation is slower in this microbenchmark (`208.29ns` vs `128.74ns`) because it pays the one-item shape check, but neither path creates threads

body:
Several Nebius-hosted models (Kimi-K2.5, DeepSeek-V3.2, GLM-5, Qwen3
thinking variants) emit hidden reasoning tokens before producing
visible output. Those tokens count against max_tokens. Empirically, a
64-token request to Kimi-K2.5 comes back with empty content because
the entire budget is consumed by reasoning, but no error is raised
and the response looks structurally fine.

Adds a "Reasoning models" subsection under Configure that lists the
known reasoning-style models, explains the implication for max_tokens
budgets, and points users at GET /v1/models for verification.

author: gghatano
body:
## 背景

`docs/reviews/action-plan.md` §3.8 Phase 4b で `domain/distance.py`（Gower 距離）が DCR / NNDR / ARD の前提として必要だが未実装。混在型データの距離関数が無く、後続の privacy 評価器が組み立てられない状態だった。

Closes #98

## この変更で提供する価値

開発者が「合成レコードと実レコードがどれだけ近いか」を **Gower 距離 1 関数で算出** でき、後続の privacy 指標 3 種（DCR/NNDR/ARD、Issue #99）の土台が揃う。

## 変更内容

- `src/synthpop_jp/domain/distance.py` 新規（185 行、TODO のみだった既存ファイルを置き換え）:
  - `gower_distance(x, y, *, is_numeric, ranges)`: 2 レコード間の純関数（Gower 1971 準拠）
  - `gower_distance_matrix(x, y, *, is_numeric, ranges=None)`: N×M 行列（vectorize、`ranges=None` で `x∪y` から自動計算）
- `tests/domain/test_distance.py` 新規（11 テスト）: 手計算 fixture / 対称性 / range=0 境界 / batch ⇔ pairwise 一致

## 影響範囲

- 変更モジュール: `domain/distance.py`（既存 stub の中身を置き換え）
- 他モジュールへの影響: なし（純粋な追加）
- 既存 API の互換性: 維持（外部から呼んでいたコードは無い）
- 依存関係の変化: なし（numpy のみ）

## テスト

- 追加テスト: 11 件
- 既存テスト維持: 627 + 11 = **638 passed, 10 skipped**

<details>
<summary>CI parity 4 コマンドの結果</summary>

\`\`\`
$ uv run ruff check .
All checks passed!

$ uv run ruff format --check .
134 files already formatted

$ uv run pyright
0 errors, 15 warnings (既存 stubs 警告のみ)

$ uv run pytest
638 passed, 10 skipped in 17.31s
\`\`\`

</details>

## 設計選択（計画 §2 から抜粋）

- **Gower 1971 の素朴定義**: 重み無し（``w_k = 1.0``）、数値: range 正規化 L1、カテゴリ: 一致/不一致
- **range=0 の挙動**: 該当属性の貢献を 0 として扱い 0 除算を避ける（Gower 1971 慣習）
- **batch API は vectorize**: numpy broadcasting で 2 重ループを排除、N=10×M=8 で pairwise 計算と数値一致を確認
- **chunk 化は不採用**: N=10,000 までは vectorize が成立。10,000 以上で必要なら別 Issue

## 残課題

- **重み付き Gower（``w_k != 1.0``）**: 別 Issue（属性間の重要度を変えたいケース）
- **chunk 化（メモリ最適化）**: 別 Issue（N=10,000 以上）
- **`gower_distance_matrix_for_pop(pop_a, pop_b)` 便宜関数**: PopulationArrays から固定属性で行列を返す高水準 API。Issue #99 の DCR 実装時に追加するのが自然なので本 PR 不採用

## レビュアーに特に見てほしい点

- `_compute_ranges` の自動 range 計算（``x ∪ y`` の合算 max-min）
- vectorize 実装が pairwise と bitwise 一致する観点（`test_matches_pairwise_calls`）
- `ranges=None` と明示指定の使い分け（DCR で base statistics を固定したい用途への配慮）

## 関連

- Issue #98（本 PR）
- Issue #99（DCR/NNDR/ARD、後続）
- spec metrics.md §5.1
- Gower (1971) "A general coefficient of similarity"
- 計画: \`docs/plans/issue-98.md\`

body:
## Summary
- Adds a metrics panel to `/backoffice/projects/$projectId` with three views over the last 30 days:
  - Top: dual-axis chart — traces (line, left axis) over manual annotations stacked positive/negative as bars (right axis).
  - Bottom-left: top-N issues table, ranked by occurrences in window (mirrors the user-facing Issues page signal — `count() FROM scores GROUP BY issue_id`). Current state badge (untracked / tracked / resolved) hydrated authoritatively from PG, not inferred from in-window events.
  - Bottom-right: 3-layer stacked-area composition — Untracked / Tracked / Resolved issue counts per day, point-in-time. `ignored_at`-stamped issues roll into Resolved.
- Lifecycle composer reconstructs each day's state from a current PG snapshot + the small set of in-window lifecycle events (issue `created_at` / `resolved_at` / `ignored_at` plus first-evaluation `created_at`). Per spec, `evaluations.archived_at` is ignored — only `deleted_at` invalidates the attachment.
- Refactored the chart layer along the way: `BarChart` and `StackedAreaChart` are gone in favour of a single composable `Chart` primitive that takes any mix of `kind: 'bar' | 'line'` (with `area`/`stack` on lines) at shared X categories. Future visual tweaks live in `metrics-section.tsx` only — no chart-package edits.
- All four backend reads (CH traces histogram, CH annotation histogram split passed/failed, CH top-issue occurrences, PG snapshot+events) fan out in parallel via `Effect.all({ concurrency: "unbounded" })`. Top-issue display details (name + current state) hydrate via a follow-up PG `inArray` keyed on the CH-returned ids.

## Test plan
- [x] `pnpm --filter @domain/admin test` — 37 passed: `getProjectMetricsUseCase` covers empty/active/clamped/window/state-hydration cases; `composeIssueLifecycleTimeline` walks the full untracked → tracked → resolved transition + the ignored-as-resolved variant + the constant-baseline path.

This is a major upgrade and refactoring of the grails-cookie plugin:

- Java target: 1.7 → implicit (via Gradle conventions)
- Gradle wrapper: 2.9 → 8.14.4 
 
## Build system refactoring
- Migrated from single-module flat build to Gradle composite build with convention plugins
- Created `build-logic/` module with 12 convention plugins for configuration as code
- Reorganized project structure:
- `plugin/` - main plugin source (src/main/groovy + src/test/groovy)
- `examples/app1/` - default-config integration tests
- `examples/app2/` - config-override integration tests
- `docs/` - Asciidoctor documentation
- `code-coverage/` - JaCoCo aggregation configuration 

## Publishing and distribution
- Migrated from Bintray to Maven Central
- Updated group: org.grails.plugins → io.github.gpc
- Updated artifact: cookie → grails-cookie
- Removed legacy Travis CI configuration
- Added GitHub Actions CI/CD workflows (build, code-coverage, code-style, release, release-notes)
- Added dependabot and renovate configuration 

## Documentation improvements
- Updated README with modern badge URLs (Maven Central, License, CI status)
- Clarified API descriptions and usage patterns
- Added snapshot build instructions
- Added SECURITY.md, issue templates, and pull request template 

## Development experience
- Added .editorconfig for consistent code formatting
- Added .sdkmanrc for Java 17 / Gradle 8.14.4 toolchain management
- Updated Gradle properties with caching, parallel builds, and build scan configuration
- Removed legacy Grails wrapper scripts (grailsw/grailsw.bat) in favor of Gradle wrapper 

## No functional changes
The plugin API and behavior remain unchanged - this is purely infrastructure, tooling, and test organization improvements to modernize the plugin for Grails 7. All configuration keys and extension methods continue to work as documented.

body:
## Summary

The 1.0.3 publish workflow ([run](https://github.com/retemper/gridsmith/actions/runs/25173971505)) finally produced a clear signal: with the stub `.npmrc` from `setup-node` removed, `pnpm changeset:publish` failed with:

```
🦋 error ENEEDAUTH This command requires you to be logged in to https://registry.npmjs.org
🦋 error You need to authorize this machine using `npm adduser`
```

Root cause: pnpm's publish path — which `@changesets/cli` calls when pnpm is the package manager — does **not** implement npm's OIDC trusted-publishing handshake. It only loads existing credentials from `.npmrc` / env vars and errors out when none are configured. There is no fallback to id-token exchange.

npm CLI 11.5+ **does** implement the handshake natively, but only when invoked directly. Replace the publish step with a tarball-based loop:

- For each non-private workspace package whose declared version is not yet on npm: `pnpm pack` to build the tarball (workspace `*` ranges are rewritten to real versions in the packed manifest), then `npm publish <tarball> --access public --provenance` to upload via the trusted-publishing path.
- Already-published versions are detected with `npm view` and skipped — matches the behavior `pnpm changeset:publish` provided.
- The git tag / GitHub Release step still iterates the same set of package.jsons, drop-in replacement.

A patch changeset is included so a 1.0.4 version PR can drive the verification (1.0.1, 1.0.2, 1.0.3 are bumped on `main` but none reached npm).

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge this PR.
- [ ] Trigger Version workflow; confirm a `chore: version packages` PR opens bumping core+react 1.0.3 → 1.0.4.
- [ ] Merge the version PR.
- [ ] Confirm the publish run reaches `npm publish <tarball>` and authenticates via OIDC against the trusted publishers.
- [ ] Confirm `npm view @gridsmith/core@1.0.4 --json | jq .dist.attestations` is non-empty.
- [ ] Confirm `npm view @gridsmith/react@1.0.4 dependencies` shows `@gridsmith/core: ^1.0.4` (workspace ranges rewritten).
- [ ] Confirm GitHub Releases for `@gridsmith/core@1.0.4` and `@gridsmith/react@1.0.4` are created.

author: jeong-sik
body:
## Summary

- **C1**: Policy-gated tool failures (`tool_not_allowed`) were misclassified as `Success` in `inferred_outcome_of_result`, causing keepers to silently skip retry/recovery. Now all `Structured_error` results are correctly `Failure`.
- **C2**: `dispatch_event` results in `record_keeper_stopped` and `record_keeper_crashed` were discarded via `ignore()`, swallowing both `Invalid_transition` and `Terminal_state` errors. Both functions now pattern-match exhaustively with appropriate logging.

## Root Cause

Silent failure audit (#silent-failure-p0) identified that:

1. `is_policy_gate_error` check in `inferred_outcome_of_result` was treating policy rejections as successful outcomes — the circuit breaker and telemetry saw no failure, so no recovery was triggered.
2. `ignore()` on `dispatch_event` in lifecycle functions meant invalid state transitions and terminal state attempts were completely invisible — no log, no metric, no recovery path.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `lib/keeper/keeper_exec_tools.ml` | Remove `is_policy_gate_error` special case; `Structured_error` → always `Failure` |
| `lib/keeper/keeper_keepalive.ml` | `record_keeper_stopped`: Replace `ignore()` with exhaustive match on both `Stop_requested` and `Drain_complete` dispatches |
| `lib/keeper/keeper_keepalive.ml` | `record_keeper_crashed`: Replace `ignore()` with exhaustive match on `Fiber_terminated` dispatch |

## Verification

- `dune build lib/keeper/` — clean, no warnings
- Exhaustive match on both error variants prevents warning 8 (partial-match)

## 📌 Refactor(api/auth): standardize CRUD patterns and harden OAuth security

## ✨ What’s Changed?

### 1. API Standardization (Events, Fields, Tags)
- **Schema Refactoring:** Standardized Pydantic models to adhere to DRY principles. `EventOut` now inherits from `EventBase`, and `TagBase` includes validation constraints for its ID.
- **CRUD/Router Decoupling:** Refactored the CRUD layer to raise standard `ValueError` exceptions instead of FastAPI's `HTTPException`. Routers now handle these errors and translate them into structured 400 responses.
- **Pattern Consistency:** Reorganized CRUD function signatures and ordering across modules to ensure a uniform developer experience.

### 2. Auth Layer Hardening
- **Dynamic Redirects:** Replaced hardcoded `localhost:8000` OAuth redirect URIs with a configurable `BACKEND_URL` in `Settings` and `.env.example`.
- **CSRF Mitigation:** Implemented secure random nonces in the OAuth `state` parameter to prevent predictable state values and enhance protection against CSRF/replay attacks.
- **Schema Documentation:** Improved the `OAuthLogin` schema with explicit descriptions to clarify that the `token` field expects the authorization code from the provider.

## 📂 Scope

- [ ] frontend
- [x] backend
- [x] common/shared
- [x] CI/config

## 📝 Notes (Optional)

- **Breaking Configuration Change:** Users must now ensure `BACKEND_URL` is correctly set in their `.env` files for OAuth callbacks to function in non-local environments. The default is set to `http://localhost:8000` for compatibility.

body:
## Summary

Third design iteration of the roster hub for PR2 of the Yahoo-Style Roster Moves plan. Incorporates the **5 user refinements** captured in [§0.5 of the plan](docs/plans/2026-04-29-yahoo-style-roster-moves-plan.md) after the v2 (PR #172) preview review.

Live at **`/design/roster-hub-v3`** (admin-only).

## v1 → v2 → v3 progression

| Version | Direction | PR |
|---------|-----------|-----|
| v1 | Standalone Swap Mode page with cards | #169 |
| v2 | Hub-and-spokes Team page with `ThemedTable` | #172 |
| **v3** | **Consolidated table + GP numbers + sub-routes** | **this PR** |

## The 5 refinements (§0.5)

1. **Consolidated table replaces hitter+pitcher stats tables.** v3 renders one `<table>` element with two sectioned `<thead>+<tbody>` pairs (Yahoo Option B). Hitters get R/HR/RBI/SB/AVG; pitchers get IP/W/SV/K/ERA/WHIP. No more separate Team.tsx stat tables in PR2.

2. **NO popup modals.** AddDrop / IL Stash / IL Activate flows render as **inline sub-routes** that replace the consolidated table while active. Page header (team name + period selector) stays visible. "← Back to roster" pill returns. PR2 wires `/teams/:code/manage/{claim,il-stash,il-activate,drop}`.

3. **Merged Position + Eligibility with games-played numbers.** New `PositionEligibilityCell` renders e.g. `[OF (12)] · 2B (3) · MI`. Primary pill (assigned slot) is interactive; secondary chips are display-only. GP suffixes use `--am-text-dim` so they're present-but-quiet. Mock data tells real stories (Mookie's Rule 2 grandfathered 2B carryover, etc).

4. **Direction confirmed.** v2's pill-as-affordance, pending row treatment, "..." menu, dnd-kit, and mobile collapse all preserved.

5. **Yahoo copy permission.** Mirroring Yahoo's pill+GP pattern directly.

## v2 → v3 diff

- ➕ `PositionEligibilityCell.tsx` — merged Pos+Eligibility with GP numbers
- ➕ `RosterHubV3.tsx` — sectioned hitter/pitcher consolidated table
- ➕ `RosterRowV3.tsx` / `MobileRowV3.tsx` — role-aware stat rendering
- ➕ `IlSectionV3.tsx` — IL section using the merged column
- ➕ `SubrouteContainer.tsx` + 4 panel mocks (`AddDropPanelMock`, `IlStashPanelMock`, `IlActivatePanelMock`, `DropPanelMock`)
- ➕ `RosterHubV3Preview.tsx` — admin preview at `/design/roster-hub-v3`
- ✏️ `types.ts` — adds `HitterStats`, `PitcherStats`, `gamesPlayedByPosition`, `RosterHubV3PreviewState`
- ✏️ `rosterHub.css` — v3 section thead, frozen first column, table-row glow via `outline` (since `box-shadow` clips at cell boundaries)
- ✏️ `RosterHubPreview.tsx` (v2) — adds "v3 with 5 refinements →" banner
- ✏️ `Docs.tsx` — description updated to point at `/design/roster-hub-v3`
- ✏️ `App.tsx` — `/design/roster-hub-v3` route added

v2 components untouched and `/design/roster-hub` still works for side-by-side comparison.

## 9 visual states (toggleable via floating panel)

1. **Idle consolidated view** — Hitters (14) + Pitchers (9) sectioned, IL (3) below
2. **Player selected** — Mookie pill clicked; OF + 2B + MI rows glow across both sections
3. **Pending swaps (3)** — Three queued; left-edge accent + tinted background + revert icon
4. **Drag in progress** — Hitter dragged → entire pitcher section dims (cross-role drops invalid)
5. **Sub-route: Add free agent** — Table replaced by inline `AddDropPanelMock`
6. **Sub-route: IL Stash** — Same pattern, `IlStashPanelMock` inline
7. **Sub-route: IL Activate** — Same pattern, `IlActivatePanelMock` inline
8. **Mobile collapsed** — Forced ≤640px, sectioned list rows, 44px touch targets
9. **Action menu open** — `…` trigger shows 5 nav items (Move / Add free agent / Stash / View / Drop)

## Judgment calls

- **Layout option B** for hitter+pitcher sectioning, per the spec recommendation. One `<table>` element, two `<thead>` + `<tbody>` pairs. Cleanest visual split, full column resolution per role, no awkward blanks.
- **Ohtani edge case** handled as DH-only hitter row. The pitcher dual-listing in OGBA's data model is a separate `Player.derivedId >= 1M` row (per the plan's filter at `syncPositionEligibility`), which would also appear as its own row with `P` slot when present. Preview keeps it simple — one row.
- **GP-less slots** (MI, CM, DH) explicitly skip the `(N)` suffix in `PositionEligibilityCell` since these are flex/structural slots with no per-position GP threshold. Eligibility derives from the underlying real position.
- **`outline` instead of `box-shadow`** for v3 row-level glow because table cells clip box-shadow at their boundaries. The v2 outline-style ring stays as the still-state for `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`.
- **No real React Router for sub-routes in preview** — toggling between the table and the panel is local state. PR2 implements the real `<Route>` mounts.

## Quality

- TypeScript strict — `cd client && npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- All 347 client tests still pass
- React.memo on `PositionEligibilityCell`, `RosterRowV3`, `MobileRowV3` — keyed on visible-state inputs
- `prefers-reduced-motion` fallback on iridescent pulse
- No backdrop-filter on animated rows (perf-oracle)

## Plan reference

§0.5 of [`docs/plans/2026-04-29-yahoo-style-roster-moves-plan.md`](docs/plans/2026-04-29-yahoo-style-roster-moves-plan.md). Don't merge — user reviews at `/design/roster-hub-v3` before PR2 starts.

- [ ] Click any position pill — verify other eligible rows glow
- [ ] Verify GP numbers render: Mookie shows `OF (47) · 2B (8)`, Trea shows `2B (38) · SS (12) · MI`, Pete shows `CM` primary with `1B (39)` chip
- [ ] Verify sub-routes: clicking "Add free agent here…" / "Stash on IL…" / "Activate from IL…" replaces the table inline (no modal)
- [ ] Resize ≤640px and verify mobile sectioned layout
- [ ] Verify v2 (`/design/roster-hub`) shows the new "v3 with 5 refinements →" banner

### 2. Created Middleware
- **File**: `src/middleware/speed-insights.middleware.js`
- **Purpose**: Automatically inject Speed Insights tracking script into HTML responses
- **Exports**:
  - `injectSpeedInsights()` - Express middleware that automatically injects the script into HTML responses
  - `getSpeedInsightsScript()` - Utility function for manual script injection

### 3. Application Integration
- **Modified**: `src/app.js`
- **Changes**:
  - Imported the Speed Insights middleware
  - Added middleware to the Express app (applies to all routes)
  - Updated the root route (`/`) to serve an HTML page instead of plain text
  - The HTML page demonstrates Speed Insights integration and provides API documentation

### 4. Documentation
- **Created**: `SPEED_INSIGHTS_SETUP.md`
- **Contents**: Comprehensive guide covering:
  - Project context (backend API vs frontend applications)
  - When Speed Insights will/won't work
  - Implementation details
  - Usage instructions
  - Vercel dashboard setup
  - Framework-specific alternatives for frontend apps
  - Recommendations for this specific project type

## Important Notes

### Project Context
This is a **Node.js/Express backend API** that primarily serves JSON responses. Vercel Speed Insights is designed for frontend applications to track client-side performance metrics (Core Web Vitals). 

### How It Works
The implementation automatically injects the Speed Insights script into any HTML responses. This means:
- ✅ Works for the root route `/` (now serves HTML)
- ✅ Will work for any future HTML pages added to the server
- ❌ Does NOT apply to JSON API endpoints (`/api/v1/auth/*`, `/api/v1/materials/*`)

### Why This Approach
Since the official Vercel documentation only provides guidance for frontend frameworks (Next.js, React, Vue, etc.) and not for Express backends, I created a middleware solution that:

body:
## Summary

Per-issue dispatch cooldown for `no_worker_process` launch failures. After a worker dies before posting any heartbeat (the failure mode driving 31+ retry storms across multiple issues from a single broken runner), `recover_failed_launch_state` writes a `<!-- dispatch-cooldown-until:<ISO> -->` audit comment. `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh::is-assigned` short-circuits with `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_ACTIVE` while the marker is unexpired, blocking dispatch from any runner — not just the one that failed.

Complementary to t2769 (3-stack circuit breaker → NMR) and t2897 (per-runner breaker, 10 events/6h). Those gates trigger after sustained failure; this gate trims the inner retry loop on a single failure.

Resolves #21892

## Changes

- `pulse-cleanup.sh`:
  - New `_post_launch_cooldown_marker(issue, slug, self_login, failure_reason)` helper. Writes a separate audit comment (not modifying the existing `CLAIM_RELEASED` comment) so the regex parse in the reader stays simple. Posts only when `failure_reason == no_worker_process` and `DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_AFTER_LAUNCH_FAILURE_SECONDS != 0` (default `1800`s = 30 min).
  - Wired into `recover_failed_launch_state` between `_post_launch_recovery_claim_released` and `_record_runner_health_zero_attempt`.
- `dispatch-dedup-helper.sh`:
  - New `_is_assigned_check_dispatch_cooldown(issue, slug)` helper. Gates on env BEFORE the gh API call (avoids one fetch per dispatch decision when feature disabled). Fetches comments, jq extracts the latest marker (`last //`-fallback over the GitHub-ordered ASC array), parses ISO with GNU `date -d` then BSD `date -j -f`/`date -r` fallbacks. Fail-open on every error path — cooldown is an optimisation, not a security gate.
  - Wired into `is_assigned` cascade (between `_is_assigned_check_no_auto_dispatch` and `_is_assigned_check_cost_budget`).
  - Wired into `enumerate_blockers` as Check 3 (after no-auto-dispatch).
- `tests/test-dispatch-cooldown.sh`: 6-case test — future marker blocks, latest of multiple wins, expired allows, no marker allows, empty array allows, feature gate `=0` skips.

## Verification

```text
$ shellcheck pulse-cleanup.sh dispatch-dedup-helper.sh tests/test-dispatch-cooldown.sh
(clean)

$ bash tests/test-dispatch-cooldown.sh
All 6 tests passed

$ bash tests/test-dispatch-dedup-no-auto-dispatch-block.sh
All 9 tests passed
```

## Tier

`tier:standard` — narrative + file refs sufficient. Insertion follows the existing `_is_assigned_check_no_auto_dispatch` pattern.

## Notes

- Default cooldown 1800s (30 min) — empirically covers the observed retry storm window without permanently blocking issues that recover. Override via env.
- Reader fail-open chosen because (a) cooldown is throttling, not security, (b) the existing 3-stack circuit breaker (t2769) and per-runner breaker (t2897) provide hard backstops, and (c) gh API contention is the most likely cooldown-check failure and should not cascade into dispatch starvation.
- Feature gate via env (`DISPATCH_COOLDOWN_AFTER_LAUNCH_FAILURE_SECONDS=0` disables both writer and reader) lets operators kill-switch without redeploy if pathology emerges.

author: atimics
body:
## Summary

Layer E of #479: a standalone CLI watchdog (`signal_verify`) that
consumes a station's chain log on disk and confirms its integrity
*without* needing a live `world_t`. Anyone — operator, third-party
auditor, future federated peer, or the on-chain verifier client
prototyped here for #480 — can independently verify signatures,
`prev_hash` linkage, monotonic `event_id`, and a small set of cross-
event invariants given just the log file and the station pubkey.

## CLI surface

```
signal_verify [options] <chain-log-path>...

Options:
  --station-pubkey=<base58>   Override pubkey (default: from filename)
  --report=<json|text>        Output format (default: text)
  --invariants=<list>         signatures,linkage,monotonic_event_id,
                              smelt_input_consumed,transfer_balanced,
                              no_orphan_events,all  (default: all)
  --strict                    Treat warnings as errors
  --since=<epoch>             Only events at or after sim tick
  --until=<epoch>             Only events up to sim tick
  --multi-station             Walk all logs together
  --registry=<file>           Optional pubkey -> name map
```

Exit semantics: `0` if all checks pass, `1` on verification failure
(or warning under `--strict`), `2` on malformed input.

## Invariant predicate framework

Six predicates ship by default. The first three are baked into
`chain_log_verify_with_pubkey()` (run in the primary pass), the
remaining three layer on top in a second pass:

| Invariant | Layer |
|---|---|
| `signatures` | core |
| `linkage` (prev_hash chain) | core |
| `monotonic_event_id` | core |
| `smelt_input_consumed` | derived |
| `transfer_balanced` | derived |
| `no_orphan_events` | derived |

`--multi-station` aggregates outputs across all supplied logs and
flags TRANSFER cargo_pubs that have no upstream output anywhere.

## Lifted API

```c
typedef struct {
    uint64_t total_events;
    uint64_t valid_events;
    uint64_t bad_signatures;
    uint64_t bad_linkage;
    uint64_t bad_payload_hash;
    uint64_t bad_authority;
    uint64_t monotonic_violations;
    uint64_t event_type_counts[CHAIN_EVT_TYPE_COUNT];
    uint64_t first_fail_event_id;
    char     first_fail_reason[128];
} chain_log_verify_report_t;

bool chain_log_verify_with_pubkey(FILE *log,
                                  const uint8_t station_pubkey[32],
                                  chain_log_verify_report_t *out);
```

The existing `chain_log_verify(const station_t *, ...)` becomes a
thin wrapper — single source of truth, two callers. The lifted core
lives in `server/chain_log_verify.c` so the standalone tool links
cleanly without dragging in `world_t` / `SIM_LOG` / station authority
dependencies. **Existing chain_log.h signatures are unchanged.**

## CI fixture + golden JSON

`tests/fixtures/3F5qRPtKg8GhGNnbd3qCj6nVJxWsGxq7pvH84okYLAqf.log`
(9.5 KB, 48 events covering all six event types) is committed
alongside its golden JSON. The new `verify-chain-logs` workflow step
builds `signal_verify` and gates on a `diff -u` against the golden.

The fixture is synthesized by `tools/gen_chain_fixture.c` from a
deterministic seed (32 × `0x42`) — *not* by running the live sim —
so sim event-semantics drift cannot silently bit-rot the fixture.
Regeneration is intentional friction (see `tests/fixtures/README.md`).

## Tests (7 new)

- `test_signal_verify_roundtrip` — emit all 6 event types, walk via lifted API.
- `test_signal_verify_byte_tamper` — flip a header byte, verifier names the event.
- `test_signal_verify_signature_corruption` — `bad_signatures == 1`.
- `test_signal_verify_mid_log_splice` — linkage / monotonic violation.
- `test_signal_verify_wrong_pubkey_rejected` — `bad_authority == 1`.
- `test_signal_verify_multi_station_independent` — each side verifies, cross fails.
- `test_signal_verify_committed_fixture` — fixture regression gate.

Total: 391 + 7 = 398 tests, all passing.

## Out of scope (deferred)

- Replay-the-sim mode (re-run ticks and assert convergence).
- Cross-server log comparison (Layer D + federation).
- On-chain anchor cross-check (#480).
- GUI / web UI.

## Test plan

- [x] `make test` passes (398/398).
- [x] `cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_TESTS_ONLY=ON && cmake --build build` clean.
- [x] `cmake -S . -B build -DBUILD_SERVER_ONLY=ON && cmake --build build` clean.
- [x] `signal_verify` runs against the committed fixture in <1s, exit 0.
- [x] `signal_verify --report=json` matches the golden JSON byte-for-byte.
- [x] `cppcheck` clean on `tools/signal_verify.c` and `server/chain_log_verify.c`.

References #479.

body:
## Changes in this pull request - ### Checklist - [ ] All unit tests pass. - [ ] All UI tests pass. - [ ] Demo project builds and runs. - [ ] I added/updated tests or detailed why my change isn't tested. - [ ] I added an entry to the `CHANGELOG.md` for any breaking changes, enhancements, or bug fixes. - [ ] I have run `ktlint` in the main directory and fixed any issues. - [ ] I have updated the SDK documentation as well as the online docs. - [ ] I have reviewed the [contributing guide](https://github.com/superwall/Superwall-Android/tree/master/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md)

Greptile Summary

This PR propagates a `timeout: Duration?` parameter through `NetworkService`, `NetworkRequestData`, and `RequestExecutor` to set `HttpURLConnection.connectTimeout` and `readTimeout`, ensuring blocking HTTP calls are bounded. Specific timeouts are wired up in `EnrichmentService` (already had a coroutine-level guard) and `SubscriptionService` (no coroutine guard). - **Effective timeout is doubled**: `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` are independent phases; setting both to `T` means the maximum HTTP-level block is `2×T`. For `SubscriptionService` calls (no coroutine-level `withTimeout`), a 5 s configured timeout can actually block for up to 10 s. - `toInt()` on `inWholeMilliseconds` silently overflows for durations > ~24.8 days; a `coerceIn` guard is a cheap safety net.

Confidence Score: 3/5

The PR improves the status quo but the doubled effective timeout at the HTTP layer means configured timeout values are not enforced as intended for SubscriptionService calls. A P1 finding (effective timeout is silently 2× the configured value for callers without a coroutine guard) pulls the score below the P1 ceiling of 4. The fix is contained to RequestExecutor and is straightforward, so it does not drop further. superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/RequestExecutor.kt — the connectTimeout/readTimeout assignment is where the doubled-timeout defect lives.

Important Files Changed

| Filename | Overview | |----------|----------| | superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/RequestExecutor.kt | Applies `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` from `NetworkRequestData.timeout`; both are set to the same value, doubling the effective maximum HTTP-level wait, and `toInt()` can silently overflow for very large durations. | | superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/NetworkRequestData.kt | Adds a non-defaulted `timeout: Duration?` field; propagated correctly through `copyWithUrl`, but missing a default value on the constructor which is a minor source-compatibility concern. | | superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/NetworkService.kt | Threads optional `timeout: Duration? = null` through `get()` and `post()` helpers into `NetworkRequestData`; looks correct. | | superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/SubscriptionService.kt | Adds explicit timeouts (10 s for `redeemToken`, 5 s for entitlement GETs) with no coroutine-level guard, so the effective maximum blocking time is 2× the configured value due to the separate `connectTimeout`/`readTimeout` issue in `RequestExecutor`. | | superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/EnrichmentService.kt | Now passes `timeout` to `post()` alongside the existing `eitherWithTimeout` coroutine guard; the coroutine guard remains the primary enforcer, with the HTTP timeouts as a safety net. | | CHANGELOG.md | Adds a changelog entry for the timeout fix; otherwise fine. |

Sequence Diagram

```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Service (Enrichment/Subscription) participant NS as NetworkService participant CE as CustomHttpUrlConnection participant RE as RequestExecutor participant HUC as HttpURLConnection S->>NS: get/post(path, timeout=T) NS->>CE: request(buildRequestData, retryCount) CE->>RE: execute(NetworkRequestData(timeout=T)) RE->>HUC: openConnection() RE->>HUC: connectTimeout = T.inWholeMilliseconds.toInt() RE->>HUC: readTimeout = T.inWholeMilliseconds.toInt() Note over HUC: Max HTTP wait = connectTimeout + readTimeout = 2×T HUC-->>RE: responseCode / data RE-->>CE: Either CE-->>NS: Either NS-->>S: Either ```
Prompt To Fix All With AI `````markdown Fix the following 3 code review issues. Work through them one at a time, proposing concise fixes. --- ### Issue 1 of 3 superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/RequestExecutor.kt:146-147 **Timeout doubled at HTTP level** `connectTimeout` and `readTimeout` are independent phases — they apply to TCP connection establishment and data read separately. Setting both to the same `timeout` value means the maximum HTTP-level blocking time is `2 × timeout`. For callers without a coroutine-level guard (e.g., `SubscriptionService.webEntitlementsByUserId` with `timeout = 5.seconds`), the call can block for up to 10 seconds instead of 5. If the intent is "the entire operation must complete within `timeout`", you'd need to split the budget or wrap every call in a coroutine-level `withTimeout` as `EnrichmentService` already does. ### Issue 2 of 3 superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/RequestExecutor.kt:146-147 **`toInt()` silently overflows for large durations** `Duration.inWholeMilliseconds` returns a `Long`; `.toInt()` truncates it without overflow protection. For any duration above ~24.8 days (`Int.MAX_VALUE` ms) the value wraps to a negative number. `HttpURLConnection` rejects negative timeouts with `IllegalArgumentException`, turning this into a runtime crash. The values used in this PR (1 s / 5 s / 10 s) are safe, but a defensive cast is cheap: ```suggestion connection.connectTimeout = timeout?.inWholeMilliseconds?.coerceIn(0, Int.MAX_VALUE.toLong())?.toInt() ?: 0 connection.readTimeout = timeout?.inWholeMilliseconds?.coerceIn(0, Int.MAX_VALUE.toLong())?.toInt() ?: 0 ``` ### Issue 3 of 3 superwall/src/main/java/com/superwall/sdk/network/NetworkRequestData.kt:20 **`timeout` parameter has no default value** All existing callsites in `NetworkService` default `timeout` to `null`, but `NetworkRequestData` itself has no default. Any direct construction of this class (e.g., in tests or future callers) now requires an explicit `timeout` argument, which is a source-breaking change. Adding `= null` makes the field consistent with how `NetworkService` exposes it. ```suggestion val timeout: Duration? = null ``` `````

author: caseyro
body:
## Summary

Implements openspec change `siyuan-mcp-reliability-fixes` to address the `No approval received.` failure pattern observed across the CDIT MCP fleet (Stolperstein KU `ku_494ce33c05e27731d2f4d9813e10100b`). The error originates above this server (Cloudflare MCP Portal, FastMCP, or Claude.ai client) — this change adds the diagnostic surface needed to disambiguate, and makes client-side retry safe by default.

### Observability

- Per-request UUIDv4 correlation ID via async-safe `ContextVar`
- Structured JSON logging: `ts`, `level`, `request_id`, `tool_name`, `caller`, `args_size_bytes`, `kernel_status`, `latency_ms`, `outcome`, `message`
- `@traced_tool` decorator wraps every registered tool
- `/health?diag=1` returns the last N (default 50) tool-call records from an in-memory ring buffer, behind the existing `/health` auth gate
- `request_id` is appended to error payloads so MCP clients can correlate failures across portal / CF Access / kernel logs

### Write-tool idempotency

- Optional `idempotency_key` on `create_document`, `append_block`, `insert_block`, `update_block`, `set_block_attrs`
- In-process `cachetools.TTLCache` (`maxsize=1024`, `ttl=300s` default)
- **Failures explicitly NOT cached** so a real retry can succeed
- Validation: `^[A-Za-z0-9_\-:.]+$`, length 1..128

### FastMCP version pinning

- `pyproject` pinned to `fastmcp==3.2.4` (with RCA comment)
- Startup logs `fastmcp_version`; mismatch logs ERROR but does not crash

### Configuration

New env vars: `SIYUAN_LOG_LEVEL`, `SIYUAN_DIAG_BUFFER_SIZE`, `SIYUAN_IDEMPOTENCY_TTL_SECONDS`.

### Documentation

- README rewritten as the canonical reference: overview + Mermaid sidecar diagram, full 29-tool catalog, transport architecture (streamable HTTP vs stdio, contrast with HTTP+SSE), FastMCP usage notes, env-var table by deploy target, Komodo deploy, single-replica caveat, `No approval received.` runbook with `curl` / `jq` recipes, FastMCP-pin rationale, local development, versioning & release pattern.
- Drift test (`tests/test_readme_tool_catalog.py`) fails CI if any registered tool is missing from the catalog.

### Tests

- 30 new tests covering observability, idempotency, `/health?diag=1`, FastMCP version guard, README drift
- Full suite: **129 passed, 6 skipped**, no regressions

## Test plan

- [x] `uv run pytest` — 129 passed, 6 skipped
- [x] `openspec validate --change siyuan-mcp-reliability-fixes` — valid
- [ ] Local Docker build smoke test
- [ ] Post-merge: pull a real `request_id` from `mcp.cdit-dev.de/.../health?diag=1` and update the README runbook example with it
- [ ] Post-merge: update Stolperstein KU `ku_494ce33c05e27731d2f4d9813e10100b`
- [ ] Cross-repo follow-ups against `klartext` portal once a `request_id` is in hand

## OpenSpec change

`openspec/changes/siyuan-mcp-reliability-fixes/` — proposal, design, specs (`request-observability`, `write-idempotency`), tasks (50/56 complete; 6 deferred for post-merge / external systems).

## Related

- Stolperstein KU `ku_494ce33c05e27731d2f4d9813e10100b` (No approval received)
- Stolperstein KU `ku_9acd350f95e2190c00cc364250976c55` (portal caching)
- CDI-821 (Flurbereinigung), CDI-948 / CDI-949 (portal auth, mcp-infra)

## Notes for reviewer

- **Failures must NOT be cached.** This is the central correctness property — verify in `mcp_siyuan/idempotency/cache.py::with_idempotency` and the parametrized tests in `tests/test_idempotency.py`.
- **Single-replica constraint**: idempotency cache and diag buffer are in-process. Documented in README and design.md. Don't horizontally scale this service.
- **FastMCP pin** is intentional for the duration of the No-approval-received RCA.

body:
💡 What: Extracted `json.dumps(message)` out of the `asyncio.gather` list comprehension in the `broadcast` method. Added `return_exceptions=True` to `gather` for safer concurrent execution.
🎯 Why: Previously, the exact same message was being JSON serialized repeatedly for every connected client inside the broadcast loop, resulting in O(N) CPU overhead on the main thread.
📊 Impact: Reduces broadcast JSON serialization overhead from O(N) to O(1) relative to connection count, freeing up event loop cycles for faster concurrency and avoiding unnecessary redundant processing.
🔬 Measurement: Benchmark the `broadcast` method with N=100 clients. Profiling will show `json.dumps` is called exactly 1 time instead of 100 times per broadcast.

author: lennoxmeldrum
body:
## Why

A student added to a class by an admin still saw "You are not yet
enrolled in a course" on `/student`. The dashboard read
`users/{uid}.courseIds` to decide what to show, but the
`setClassMembers` action only mirrors `classIds` onto the user doc —
`courseIds` is initialised to `[]` at signup and never updated.

## What

Drop the dependency on the `courseIds` mirrored field; derive the
course list at read time:

1. Query `classes where studentIds array-contains uid` (one read).
2. Dedupe the resulting `courseId`s.
3. `getAll()` the course docs in one batch read.
4. Filter archived classes **in memory** so we don't need a composite
   index — `array-contains` + a second `==` filter requires one, and
   `deploy-dev.yml` doesn't auto-apply indexes (see
   `DEPLOY_CORRECTIONS.md` PRs #21/#23). A student is in at most a
   handful of classes; the cost is negligible.

Single source of truth for enrolment is now the class document, not a
mirrored field that drifts.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npm run build` clean

## Not changed (intentional)

- The `courseIds: []` field still gets initialised on the user doc at
  signup (`app/api/auth/session/route.ts`). It's harmless dead state
  and removing it is a separate cleanup.
- The teacher dashboard already queries classes directly via
  `teacherIds`, so it's unaffected.

## After merge

Auto-deploys to dev (~5 min). Sign in as the test students again — the
AP PCM course should now appear on `/student`.
